name: Prophet Muhammad ﷺ
title: Seal of the Prophets
bio: The final Messenger of Allah, born in Mecca around 570 CE. He received the first revelation at the age of 40 and led the Muslim community from Mecca to Medina until his passing in 632 CE.

name: Prophet Adam
title: The First Man
bio: The first human being and the first prophet, created by Allah from clay. He and his wife lived in Paradise before being sent down to the earth.

name: Prophet Idris
title: The Truthful
bio: Mentioned in the Quran as a truthful prophet whom Allah raised to a high station.

name: Prophet Nuh
title: The Ark Builder
bio: Called his people to worship Allah alone for 950 years, according to the Quran. By Allah's command he built the ark that saved the believers from the flood.

name: Prophet Hud
title: Messenger to Ad
bio: Sent to the people of Ad, a mighty nation who rejected his call and were destroyed by a violent wind.

name: Prophet Salih
title: Messenger to Thamud
bio: Sent to the people of Thamud, who were given a miraculous she-camel as a sign. They harmed her and were struck by punishment.

name: Prophet Ibrahim
title: Khalilullah, Friend of Allah
bio: Rejected the idols of his people and was tested with great trials. With his son Ismail he raised the foundations of the Kaaba.

name: Prophet Lut
title: Warner of His People
bio: Sent to a people who committed grave sins. He and his family, except his wife, were saved when the punishment came.

name: Prophet Ismail
title: True to His Promise
bio: Son of Ibrahim, described in the Quran as true to his promise. He helped his father build the Kaaba in Mecca.

name: Prophet Ishaq
title: Blessed Son of Ibrahim
bio: Son of Ibrahim and father of Yaqub, given as glad tidings to his parents in their old age.

name: Prophet Yaqub
title: The Patient Father
bio: Son of Ishaq and father of Yusuf and his brothers. He showed beautiful patience when he lost his son Yusuf.

name: Prophet Yusuf
title: The Interpreter of Dreams
bio: Betrayed by his brothers and imprisoned unjustly, he was given knowledge of dream interpretation and rose to authority in Egypt.

name: Prophet Ayyub
title: The Patient
bio: Tested with severe illness and loss, he remained patient and turned to Allah, who restored his health and blessings.

name: Prophet Shuayb
title: Messenger to Madyan
bio: Sent to the people of Madyan, whom he urged to worship Allah alone and to deal honestly in weights and measures.

name: Prophet Musa
title: Kalimullah, Spoke with Allah
bio: The prophet most often mentioned in the Quran. He confronted Pharaoh and led the Children of Israel out of Egypt.

name: Prophet Harun
title: Helper of Musa
bio: The brother of Musa, whom Allah appointed as his helper and spokesman.

name: Prophet Dhul-Kifl
title: The Patient and Righteous
bio: Mentioned in the Quran among the patient and the righteous servants of Allah.

name: Prophet Dawud
title: King and Prophet
bio: Received the Zabur and was given wisdom and kingship. As a young man he defeated the tyrant Jalut (Goliath).

name: Prophet Sulayman
title: The Wise King
bio: Son of Dawud, granted a unique kingdom by Allah, including authority over the wind and understanding of the speech of birds.

name: Prophet Ilyas
title: Opponent of Idolatry
bio: Called his people to leave the worship of Ba'l and to worship Allah alone.

name: Prophet al-Yasa
title: Among the Chosen
bio: Mentioned in the Quran among the chosen and the best of people.

name: Prophet Yunus
title: Dhun-Nun, Companion of the Fish
bio: Swallowed by a great fish after leaving his people. In the darkness he glorified Allah and was saved.

name: Prophet Zakariyya
title: Guardian of Maryam
bio: Cared for Maryam and prayed for a child in his old age. Allah answered him with the gift of Yahya.

name: Prophet Yahya
title: The Pure
bio: Son of Zakariyya, given wisdom and purity from his youth, and known for his devotion and kindness.

name: Prophet Isa
title: Al-Masih, Son of Maryam
bio: Born miraculously to Maryam and sent to the Children of Israel with the Injil. He performed miracles by Allah's permission.

name: Abu Bakr as-Siddiq
title: The Truthful, First Caliph
bio: The closest companion of the Prophet ﷺ, who accompanied him during the Hijrah. He became the first caliph (632-634 CE) and held the community together after the Prophet's passing.

name: Umar ibn al-Khattab
title: Al-Faruq, Second Caliph
bio: Second caliph (634-644 CE), known for his strict justice. Under his leadership the state expanded greatly and many administrative systems were established.

name: Uthman ibn Affan
title: Third Caliph
bio: Third caliph (644-656 CE), known for his modesty and generosity. He oversaw the creation of standard written copies of the Quran.

name: Ali ibn Abi Talib
title: Fourth Caliph
bio: Cousin and son-in-law of the Prophet ﷺ, and one of the first to accept Islam. Famed for his courage, knowledge and eloquence, he was the fourth caliph (656-661 CE).

name: Khalid ibn al-Walid
title: Sayfullah, the Sword of Allah
bio: A brilliant military commander who never lost a battle after accepting Islam. He led decisive campaigns in Iraq and Syria, including the Battle of Yarmouk.

name: Hamza ibn Abdul-Muttalib
title: Lion of Allah
bio: Uncle of the Prophet ﷺ and one of the bravest warriors of Quraysh. He fought at Badr and was martyred at the Battle of Uhud in 625 CE.

name: Khadija bint Khuwaylid
title: Mother of the Believers
bio: The first wife of the Prophet ﷺ and a successful merchant. She was the first to believe in his message and supported him through the hardest years in Mecca.

name: Aisha bint Abi Bakr
title: Mother of the Believers
bio: A wife of the Prophet ﷺ and a renowned scholar. She narrated a large number of hadiths and taught many students after the Prophet's passing.

name: Fatima az-Zahra
title: Daughter of the Prophet
bio: The youngest daughter of the Prophet ﷺ and wife of Ali. She is the mother of Hasan and Husayn and is remembered for her piety and patience.

name: Bilal ibn Rabah
title: The First Muadhdhin
bio: Born into slavery, he endured torture in Mecca for refusing to abandon his faith. He was freed by Abu Bakr and became the first caller to prayer in Islam.

name: Abu Hurayra
title: Narrator of Hadith
bio: A companion who stayed close to the Prophet ﷺ in Medina and became one of the most prolific narrators of hadith.

name: Abdullah ibn Abbas
title: Interpreter of the Quran
bio: Cousin of the Prophet ﷺ, known as the scholar of the Ummah for his knowledge of Quranic interpretation. He was still young when the Prophet ﷺ passed away.

name: Al-Hasan ibn Ali
title: Grandson of the Prophet
bio: The elder grandson of the Prophet ﷺ. After his father's death he gave up the caliphate to unite the Muslims.

name: Al-Husayn ibn Ali
title: Grandson of the Prophet
bio: The younger grandson of the Prophet ﷺ, martyred at Karbala in 680 CE (61 AH).

name: Salman al-Farisi
title: The Seeker of Truth
bio: A Persian companion who travelled far in search of the truth. He suggested digging the trench that protected Medina during the Battle of the Trench in 627 CE.

name: Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas
title: The Archer of Islam
bio: One of the earliest Muslims and among the ten promised Paradise. He commanded the Muslim army at the Battle of al-Qadisiyyah against the Persian Empire.

name: Abu Ubayda ibn al-Jarrah
title: Trustworthy of the Ummah
bio: One of the ten promised Paradise, known for his honesty and humility. He led the Muslim armies in the conquest of Syria.

name: Az-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam
title: Disciple of the Prophet
bio: A cousin of the Prophet ﷺ and one of the ten promised Paradise. He was a fearless horseman who fought in nearly all the major battles of the era.

name: Talha ibn Ubaydullah
title: The Shield at Uhud
bio: One of the ten promised Paradise. At the Battle of Uhud he shielded the Prophet ﷺ and suffered many wounds defending him.

name: Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf
title: The Generous Merchant
bio: One of the ten promised Paradise and a gifted trader who built a fortune in Medina. He gave very large sums in charity and for the defense of the community.

name: Abdullah ibn Umar
title: Follower of the Sunnah
bio: Son of Umar, famed for closely following the example of the Prophet ﷺ and for narrating many hadiths.

name: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud
title: Teacher of the Quran
bio: One of the earliest Muslims and among the most knowledgeable companions in the Quran. He later taught the people of Kufa.

name: Anas ibn Malik
title: Servant of the Prophet
bio: Served the Prophet ﷺ for ten years from his childhood in Medina and narrated many hadiths.

name: Mu'adh ibn Jabal
title: Knower of Halal and Haram
bio: A young companion from Medina whom the Prophet ﷺ praised for his knowledge of the lawful and the forbidden, and sent to teach in Yemen.

name: Zayd ibn Thabit
title: Scribe of the Revelation
bio: A young scribe of the Prophet ﷺ who led the collection of the Quran in written form after the Prophet's passing.

name: Abu Dharr al-Ghifari
title: The Truth-Teller
bio: An early convert known for his honesty, simple living and plain speech.

name: Umm Salama
title: Mother of the Believers
bio: A wife of the Prophet ﷺ, known for her wisdom and the sound advice she gave at Hudaybiyyah. She migrated to Abyssinia and later to Medina.

name: Mus'ab ibn Umayr
title: The First Ambassador
bio: Raised in comfort in Mecca, he gave up wealth for his faith. He was sent to Medina to teach Islam before the Hijrah and was martyred carrying the banner at Uhud.

name: Ja'far ibn Abi Talib
title: Leader of the Migration to Abyssinia
bio: Cousin of the Prophet ﷺ and spokesman of the Muslims who migrated to Abyssinia. He was martyred at the Battle of Mu'tah in 629 CE.

name: Amr ibn al-As
title: Conqueror of Egypt
bio: A skilled commander and strategist who led the Muslim conquest of Egypt around 640 CE and founded the city of Fustat.

name: Ammar ibn Yasir
title: Steadfast in Hardship
bio: An early convert who endured severe persecution in Mecca together with his parents, Yasir and Sumayyah. He remained a loyal companion until his death at Siffin in 657 CE.

name: Hudhayfa ibn al-Yaman
title: Keeper of the Secrets
bio: A companion trusted by the Prophet ﷺ with knowledge about the hypocrites. He was sent on a night mission during the Battle of the Trench.

name: Abu Ayyub al-Ansari
title: Host of the Prophet
bio: The Medinan companion in whose house the Prophet ﷺ first stayed after the Hijrah. He kept fighting in the way of Allah into old age.

name: Sa'd ibn Mu'adh
title: Leader of the Aws
bio: Chief of the Aws tribe in Medina and a strong supporter of the Prophet ﷺ. He died from a wound received at the Battle of the Trench.

name: Sumayyah bint Khayyat
title: The First Martyr
bio: An early Muslim woman of Mecca who endured torture for her faith and is remembered as the first martyr in Islam.

name: Asma bint Abi Bakr
title: She of the Two Belts
bio: Daughter of Abu Bakr who brought food and supplies to the Prophet ﷺ and her father during the Hijrah. She is known as Dhat an-Nitaqayn.

name: Nusayba bint Ka'b
title: Defender at Uhud
bio: Also known as Umm Ammara, a brave woman of Medina who fought to protect the Prophet ﷺ at the Battle of Uhud.

name: Hafsa bint Umar
title: Mother of the Believers
bio: A wife of the Prophet ﷺ and daughter of Umar. She kept the written copy of the Quran compiled under Abu Bakr.

name: Ubayy ibn Ka'b
title: Master of Reciters
bio: A companion from Medina and scribe of the Prophet ﷺ, named among the best reciters of the Quran.

name: Muhammad al-Fatih
title: Conqueror of Constantinople
bio: Ottoman sultan who conquered Constantinople in 1453 CE at about the age of 21.

name: Salah ad-Din al-Ayyubi
title: Liberator of Jerusalem
bio: Founder of the Ayyubid dynasty. After the victory at Hattin he recaptured Jerusalem in 1187 CE and was admired for his chivalry and mercy.

name: Tariq ibn Ziyad
title: Conqueror of Al-Andalus
bio: An Umayyad general who crossed into the Iberian Peninsula in 711 CE. His campaign began the Muslim rule of Al-Andalus.

name: Sayf ad-Din Qutuz
title: Victor of Ain Jalut
bio: Mamluk sultan who defeated the Mongol army at the Battle of Ain Jalut in 1260 CE.

name: Baibars
title: Sultan of the Mamluks
bio: A commander at Ain Jalut who later became Mamluk sultan and recovered many strongholds from the Crusaders.

name: Uqba ibn Nafi
title: Founder of Kairouan
bio: Umayyad commander who led conquests in North Africa and founded the city of Kairouan around 670 CE.

name: Muhammad ibn al-Qasim
title: Young General of Sindh
bio: A young Umayyad commander who led the conquest of Sindh around 711 CE.

name: Yusuf ibn Tashfin
title: Victor of Zallaqa
bio: Almoravid leader who crossed into Al-Andalus and defeated Alfonso VI at the Battle of Zallaqa in 1086 CE.

name: Omar al-Mukhtar
title: Lion of the Desert
bio: Libyan teacher of the Quran and resistance leader who fought Italian colonial rule for over twenty years until his execution in 1931.

name: Emir Abdelkader
title: Emir of the Algerian Resistance
bio: Algerian scholar and leader who resisted the French conquest of Algeria from 1832 to 1847.

name: Nur ad-Din Zangi
title: Unifier of Syria
bio: Ruler of Syria who united Muslim lands against the Crusaders and paved the way for Salah ad-Din.

name: Musa ibn Nusayr
title: Governor of Ifriqiya
bio: Umayyad governor of North Africa who oversaw the expansion into the Maghreb and the conquest of Al-Andalus.

name: Imam Abu Hanifa
title: Imam of the Hanafi School
bio: Al-Nu'man ibn Thabit (d. 767 CE), founder of the Hanafi school and a leading jurist of Kufa and Baghdad.

name: Imam Malik ibn Anas
title: Imam of Medina
bio: Founder of the Maliki school (d. 795 CE) and author of the Muwatta, one of the earliest collections of hadith and fiqh.

name: Imam ash-Shafi'i
title: Founder of Usul al-Fiqh
bio: Muhammad ibn Idris ash-Shafi'i (d. 820 CE), founder of the Shafi'i school and author of ar-Risala on the principles of jurisprudence.

name: Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal
title: Imam of Ahl as-Sunnah
bio: Founder of the Hanbali school (d. 855 CE) and compiler of the Musnad. He was imprisoned and tortured for refusing to say that the Quran is created.

name: Imam al-Bukhari
title: Compiler of Sahih al-Bukhari
bio: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Bukhari (d. 870 CE), whose Sahih is regarded as the most authentic collection of hadith.

name: Ibn Taymiyyah
title: Sheikh al-Islam
bio: Hanbali scholar (d. 1328 CE) who wrote extensively on creed and jurisprudence and defended the way of the Salaf.

name: Imam Muslim
title: Compiler of Sahih Muslim
bio: Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj (d. 875 CE), author of Sahih Muslim, the second most revered collection of hadith.

name: Abu Dawud as-Sijistani
title: Author of Sunan Abi Dawud
bio: Hadith scholar (d. 889 CE) who compiled the Sunan, with a focus on hadiths of legal rulings.

name: Imam at-Tirmidhi
title: Author of Jami at-Tirmidhi
bio: Hadith scholar (d. 892 CE) who compiled the Jami, noting the grades of hadiths and the views of the jurists.

name: Imam an-Nasa'i
title: Author of Sunan an-Nasa'i
bio: Hadith scholar (d. 915 CE) known for his strict conditions in accepting narrators.

name: Imam Ibn Majah
title: Author of Sunan Ibn Majah
bio: Hadith scholar from Qazvin (d. 887 CE) whose Sunan is counted among the six major collections.

name: Ibn al-Qayyim
title: Student of Ibn Taymiyyah
bio: Hanbali scholar (d. 1350 CE) famed for his works on the heart and on Prophetic guidance, such as Zad al-Ma'ad.

name: Ibn Kathir
title: Mufassir and Historian
bio: Scholar (d. 1373 CE) who wrote a famous commentary on the Quran and the history al-Bidaya wa'n-Nihaya.

name: Adh-Dhahabi
title: Historian of Scholars
bio: Scholar (d. 1348 CE) known for Siyar A'lam an-Nubala and his works on hadith narrators and Islamic history.

name: Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani
title: Commentator of Sahih al-Bukhari
bio: Hadith scholar (d. 1449 CE) who wrote Fath al-Bari, the best-known commentary on Sahih al-Bukhari.

name: Abd al-Aziz ibn Baz
title: Grand Mufti of Saudi Arabia
bio: Scholar (1912-1999 CE) who served as Grand Mufti of Saudi Arabia and was known for his teaching and fatwas.

name: Muhammad Nasir ad-Din al-Albani
title: Scholar of Hadith
bio: Scholar (1914-1999 CE) born in Albania and known for his work in grading hadiths.

name: Ibn Rajab al-Hanbali
title: Scholar of Hadith and the Heart
bio: Hanbali scholar (d. 1393 CE), author of Jami' al-'Ulum wa'l-Hikam, a commentary on forty hadiths.

name: Ibn Qudama al-Maqdisi
title: Author of al-Mughni
bio: Hanbali jurist (d. 1223 CE) who wrote al-Mughni, a major work of comparative jurisprudence.

name: Ibn Abd al-Barr
title: Hafiz of Al-Andalus
bio: Maliki scholar of Al-Andalus (d. 1071 CE), known for at-Tamhid and al-Isti'ab on the companions.

name: Sufyan ath-Thawri
title: Leader of the Hadith Scholars
bio: Early scholar of Kufa (d. 778 CE), a leading hadith narrator and jurist known for his piety.

name: Imam al-Awza'i
title: Imam of the Levant
bio: Scholar of Syria (d. 774 CE) whose legal school was followed for a time in the Levant and Al-Andalus.

name: Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak
title: Scholar and Mujahid
bio: Scholar of Khurasan (d. 797 CE), known for his knowledge of hadith, his generosity and his service on the frontiers.

name: Muhammad ibn Salih al-Uthaymeen
title: Scholar of Unayzah
bio: Scholar (1929-2001 CE) from Qassim in Saudi Arabia, known for his teaching and his explanations of fiqh and creed.

name: The First Revelation
title: The Cave of Hira
bio: In the cave of Hira near Mecca, around 610 CE, the angel Jibril brought the first verses of the Quran to the Prophet ﷺ, beginning with the command "Read" (Iqra).

name: The Night Journey and Ascension
title: From Mecca to Jerusalem and the Heavens
bio: In a single night, before the Hijrah, the Prophet ﷺ was taken from the Sacred Mosque in Mecca to al-Aqsa in Jerusalem, then ascended through the heavens. The five daily prayers were prescribed on this journey.

name: The Migration to Abyssinia
title: Refuge Under the Negus
bio: Around 615 CE a group of persecuted Muslims left Mecca for Abyssinia, where the just king an-Najashi gave them protection. Ja'far ibn Abi Talib spoke for them before the king.

name: The Second Pledge of al-Aqaba
title: The Pledge of Medina
bio: Shortly before the Hijrah, a delegation from Medina pledged at al-Aqaba, near Mecca, to protect the Prophet ﷺ as they would protect their own families, which opened the way to the migration.

name: The Hijrah
title: Migration to Medina
bio: In 622 CE the Prophet ﷺ left Mecca with Abu Bakr and sheltered in the cave of Thawr before reaching Medina. This migration marks the start of the Hijri calendar, introduced later under Umar.

name: Battle of Badr
title: The Day of Criterion
bio: Fought in Ramadan 2 AH (624 CE), the first major battle of Islam. Around 313 Muslims faced a Qurayshi army about three times larger and won a decisive victory.

name: Battle of Uhud
title: The Lesson of Obedience
bio: Fought in 3 AH (625 CE) near the mountain of Uhud, north of Medina. The Muslims were close to victory until a group of archers left their post. Hamza was martyred in this battle.

name: Battle of the Trench
title: The Siege of Medina
bio: In 5 AH (627 CE) a coalition of tribes besieged Medina. On the advice of Salman al-Farisi the Muslims dug a trench around the exposed side of the city, and the siege failed.

name: Treaty of Hudaybiyyah
title: The Clear Victory
bio: In 6 AH (628 CE) the Prophet ﷺ and Quraysh agreed to a ten-year truce near Mecca. The treaty looked unfavorable to many Muslims, but the Quran called it a clear victory, and it paved the way to the conquest of Mecca.

name: Battle of Khaybar
title: The Fortresses of the North
bio: In 7 AH the Muslims marched against the fortified settlements of Khaybar, an oasis north of Medina, and took them after a campaign that lasted several days.

name: Battle of Mu'tah
title: The Three Commanders
bio: In 8 AH (629 CE) a small Muslim army met a far larger Byzantine force. Zayd ibn Haritha, Ja'far ibn Abi Talib and Abdullah ibn Rawaha were martyred in turn, and Khalid ibn al-Walid took command and saved the army.

name: Conquest of Mecca
title: The Great Opening
bio: In 8 AH (630 CE) the Prophet ﷺ entered Mecca with a large army almost without fighting. The idols around the Kaaba were removed, and he forgave the people of Quraysh.

name: Battle of Hunayn
title: The Valley Between Mecca and Ta'if
bio: Soon after the conquest of Mecca, the Muslims faced the tribes of Hawazin and Thaqif in the valley of Hunayn. They were shaken at first, then regrouped around the Prophet ﷺ and won.

name: Expedition of Tabuk
title: The Army of Hardship
bio: In 9 AH (630 CE) the Prophet ﷺ led a large army north in the heat of summer to face Byzantine forces. No battle took place, but the expedition showed the strength of the Muslim state.

name: The Farewell Pilgrimage
title: The Sermon at Arafat
bio: In 10 AH (632 CE) the Prophet ﷺ performed his only Hajj and gave his farewell sermon at Arafat, stressing the sanctity of life and property and the rights of all people before Allah.

name: Battle of Yamama
title: War Against the False Prophet
bio: Fought in 632-633 CE under Abu Bakr against the followers of Musaylima, who claimed to be a prophet. Many reciters of the Quran fell, which led to the first written compilation of the Quran.

name: Battle of Yarmouk
title: Decisive Victory in the Levant
bio: In 636 CE the Muslim army under Khalid ibn al-Walid and Abu Ubayda defeated a much larger Byzantine army by the Yarmouk river, opening the way for the conquest of the Levant.

name: Battle of al-Qadisiyyah
title: The Fall of the Sasanian Frontier
bio: Around 636 CE the Muslim army led by Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas defeated the Sasanian Persian army in Iraq after several days of fighting, a turning point in the conquest of Persia.

name: Battle of Guadalete
title: The Gate to Al-Andalus
bio: In 711 CE Tariq ibn Ziyad defeated the Visigothic king Roderic in southern Iberia, a victory that started the Muslim presence in Al-Andalus.

name: Battle of az-Zallaqa
title: The Almoravids Cross the Strait
bio: In 1086 CE Yusuf ibn Tashfin crossed from North Africa to help the Andalusian rulers and defeated the army of Alfonso VI of Castile near Badajoz.

name: Battle of Hattin
title: Road to Jerusalem
bio: In 1187 CE Salah ad-Din crushed the Crusader army near Tiberias. Jerusalem was recaptured a few months later without a massacre.

name: Battle of Ain Jalut
title: The Mongols Are Stopped
bio: In 1260 CE the Mamluk army under Qutuz, with Baibars among its commanders, defeated the Mongols in Palestine, ending their advance toward Egypt.

name: Conquest of Constantinople
title: The Prophecy Fulfilled
bio: In 1453 CE the Ottoman sultan Muhammad al-Fatih took Constantinople after a siege of about 53 days, ending the Byzantine Empire and fulfilling a long-awaited hope of the Muslims.

name: Sa'id ibn Zayd
title: One of the Ten Promised Paradise
bio: An early Muslim and brother-in-law of Umar. His father Zayd ibn Amr rejected idol worship even before Islam. He later took part in the conquest of Syria.

name: Abu Sufyan ibn Harb
title: Leader of Quraysh
bio: A leader of Quraysh who led the opposition to the Muslims at Uhud and the Trench. He accepted Islam at the conquest of Mecca in 8 AH and later fought in the Levant.

name: Al-Abbas ibn Abdul-Muttalib
title: Uncle of the Prophet
bio: An uncle of the Prophet ﷺ who gave him support in Mecca and accepted Islam before the conquest. He was the ancestor of the Abbasid caliphs.

name: Abdullah ibn az-Zubayr
title: First Child Born After the Hijrah
bio: Born in Medina soon after the Hijrah, the first Muslim child born there. He was proclaimed caliph in Mecca and died defending the city in 73 AH.

name: Abdullah ibn Rawaha
title: Poet and Commander
bio: A poet of the Ansar and one of the chiefs at the pledge of al-Aqaba. He was martyred as the third commander at the Battle of Mu'tah.

name: Zayd ibn Haritha
title: Beloved of the Prophet
bio: Freed by the Prophet ﷺ and raised in his household, he is the only companion named in the Quran. He commanded Muslim expeditions and fell at Mu'tah.

name: Usama ibn Zayd
title: Young Commander
bio: Son of Zayd ibn Haritha, appointed by the Prophet ﷺ to lead an army toward the Byzantine frontier while still very young. Abu Bakr sent the army out after the Prophet's passing.

name: Abu Talha al-Ansari
title: Archer of the Ansar
bio: A skilled archer of Medina who stood close to the Prophet ﷺ at Uhud and shielded him. He was known for his generosity and his orchard Bayruha.

name: Umm Sulaym bint Milhan
title: Mother of Anas
bio: A woman of the Ansar who accepted Islam early and raised her son Anas in devotion to the Prophet ﷺ. She is remembered for her wisdom and patience.

name: Sa'd ibn Ubada
title: Chief of the Khazraj
bio: A leader of the Khazraj tribe in Medina and a generous supporter of the Prophet ﷺ. He took part in the pledge of al-Aqaba.

name: Ubada ibn as-Samit
title: Teacher of the Quran
bio: A companion from the Ansar who attended the pledges of al-Aqaba and fought at Badr. He taught the Quran in Medina and later served as a judge in Syria.

name: Abu Musa al-Ash'ari
title: The Beautiful Reciter
bio: A companion from Yemen known for his beautiful recitation of the Quran. He served as governor of Basra and Kufa under Umar and Uthman.

name: Al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba
title: Governor of Kufa
bio: A companion known for his political skill, who served as governor of Basra and Kufa. He was present at Hudaybiyyah and joined the conquests in Iraq.

name: Hassan ibn Thabit
title: Poet of the Prophet
bio: The main poet of the Muslims in Medina, who answered the verses of the Prophet's enemies. He lived long and was respected for his eloquence.

name: Khabbab ibn al-Aratt
title: Steadfast Under Torture
bio: An early convert in Mecca who was a blacksmith and endured painful torture for his faith. He remained a respected companion until his death in Kufa.

name: Suhayb ar-Rumi
title: The Generous Emigrant
bio: A merchant raised among the Byzantines who joined Islam early. He gave up all his wealth to migrate to Medina, and the Prophet ﷺ was pleased with him.

name: Uthman ibn Maz'un
title: The First Emigrant to Die in Medina
bio: An early Muslim known for his devotion and restraint. He migrated to Abyssinia and then to Medina, where he was the first of the emigrants to pass away.

name: Abdullah ibn Salam
title: Scholar Who Accepted Islam
bio: A respected Jewish scholar of Medina who accepted Islam when the Prophet ﷺ arrived. He narrated knowledge from the earlier scriptures and is among the well-known companions.

name: Abu ad-Darda
title: The Wise of Damascus
bio: A companion from Medina admired for his wisdom and worship. He moved to Syria, taught the Quran in Damascus and served there as a judge.

name: Shurahbil ibn Hasana
title: Commander in Syria
bio: A companion who migrated to Abyssinia and later commanded Muslim forces in the conquest of Syria. He died in the plague of Amwas.

name: Yazid ibn Abi Sufyan
title: Commander in the Levant
bio: A commander sent by Abu Bakr to Syria, who led one of the main armies of the conquest. He governed Damascus and died in the plague of Amwas.

name: Al-Qa'qa' ibn Amr
title: Hero of al-Qadisiyyah
bio: A fearless horseman who fought in Iraq and became famous at al-Qadisiyyah. The caliphs reportedly valued his presence in an army at a thousand men.

name: Al-Muthanna ibn Haritha
title: Pioneer in Iraq
bio: A commander of the tribe of Shayban who began the Muslim campaigns in southern Iraq before the arrival of Khalid. He paved the way for al-Qadisiyyah.

name: Ikrima ibn Abi Jahl
title: Convert and Commander
bio: Son of Abu Jahl who opposed Islam at first but accepted it at the conquest of Mecca. He served in the Ridda wars and was martyred fighting in the Levant.

name: Jabir ibn Abdullah
title: Narrator of Hadith
bio: A young companion from Medina who attended the pledge of al-Aqaba and many later battles. He narrated a large number of hadiths, including a detailed account of the Prophet's Hajj.

name: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri
title: Narrator from the Ansar
bio: A young companion from Medina who took part in campaigns after Uhud and became a well-known narrator of hadith. He was known for his knowledge and honesty.

name: Zayd ibn al-Khattab
title: Brother of Umar
bio: The elder brother of Umar, a brave fighter who accepted Islam before him. He carried the banner at the Battle of Yamama and was martyred there.

name: Salim Mawla Abi Hudhayfa
title: Master Reciter
bio: A freed slave who became one of the finest reciters of the Quran, one of those the Prophet ﷺ told people to learn from. He was martyred at Yamama.

name: Jarir ibn Abdullah
title: The Handsome Companion
bio: A leader of the tribe of Bajila who accepted Islam in the last years of the Prophet's life. He later took part in the conquest of Iraq.

name: Adi ibn Hatim
title: Son of the Generous Hatim
bio: A noble of the tribe of Tayy and son of the famous generous poet Hatim. He accepted Islam in 9 AH and stayed loyal to Abu Bakr during the Ridda wars.

name: Al-Bara ibn Azib
title: Young Narrator and Fighter
bio: A companion who was too young for Badr but took part in many later campaigns, including the conquest of Rayy. He narrated many hadiths.

name: An-Nu'man ibn Muqarrin
title: Commander at Nahavand
bio: A companion who led the Muslim army in Persia at the battle of Nahavand, known as the victory of victories. He was martyred in the battle.

name: Abdullah ibn Jahsh
title: Leader of the Nakhla Expedition
bio: A cousin of the Prophet ﷺ who migrated to Abyssinia and then Medina. He led the first expedition to Nakhla and was martyred at Uhud.

name: Tamim ad-Dari
title: The Christian Who Embraced Islam
bio: A companion from Palestine who had been a Christian and accepted Islam in 9 AH. The Prophet ﷺ narrated a story he told about the Antichrist.

name: Ubayda ibn al-Harith
title: First to Duel at Badr
bio: A cousin of the Prophet ﷺ and one of the earliest Muslims. He was among the first to face the enemy in single combat at Badr and died of his wounds.

name: Amir ibn Fuhayra
title: Helper During the Hijrah
bio: A freed servant of Abu Bakr who helped the Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr on the Hijrah by bringing them food and covering their tracks. He was martyred at Bi'r Ma'una.

name: Abu Salama ibn Abd al-Asad
title: The First to Migrate to Medina
bio: A cousin of the Prophet ﷺ who migrated to Abyssinia and then became one of the first to reach Medina. His widow Umm Salama later married the Prophet ﷺ.

name: Sawda bint Zam'a
title: Mother of the Believers
bio: A wife of the Prophet ﷺ who married him after the death of Khadija. She migrated to Abyssinia and then Medina and was known for her kindness.

name: Zaynab bint Jahsh
title: Mother of the Believers
bio: A wife of the Prophet ﷺ and cousin of his, known for her generosity and for working with her hands to give in charity.

name: Zaynab bint Khuzayma
title: Mother of the Poor
bio: A wife of the Prophet ﷺ called Umm al-Masakin for her care for the poor. She passed away only a short time after the marriage.

name: Juwayriyya bint al-Harith
title: Mother of the Believers
bio: A noblewoman of the tribe of Mustaliq who became a wife of the Prophet ﷺ. Many of her people were freed and accepted Islam because of this marriage.

name: Safiyya bint Huyayy
title: Mother of the Believers
bio: A wife of the Prophet ﷺ who came from the tribe of Banu Nadir. She was known for her patience, knowledge and generosity.

name: Umm Habiba bint Abi Sufyan
title: Mother of the Believers
bio: A daughter of Abu Sufyan who accepted Islam early and migrated to Abyssinia, where she was married to the Prophet ﷺ. She stayed firm while her father still opposed him.

name: Maymuna bint al-Harith
title: Mother of the Believers
bio: A wife of the Prophet ﷺ, married in 7 AH during the pilgrimage. She was the last of his wives to marry him.

name: Ruqayya bint Muhammad
title: Daughter of the Prophet
bio: A daughter of the Prophet ﷺ and wife of Uthman. She migrated to Abyssinia and then to Medina, where she died around the time of Badr.

name: Umm Kulthum bint Muhammad
title: Daughter of the Prophet
bio: A daughter of the Prophet ﷺ who married Uthman after the death of her sister Ruqayya. She passed away in 9 AH.

name: Zaynab bint Muhammad
title: Eldest Daughter of the Prophet
bio: The eldest daughter of the Prophet ﷺ. She stayed in Mecca for some time after the Hijrah before joining her father in Medina.

name: Safiyya bint Abdul-Muttalib
title: Aunt of the Prophet
bio: An aunt of the Prophet ﷺ and mother of az-Zubayr. She stood by the Muslims at Uhud and defended the women's fortress during the siege of the Trench.

name: Umm Ayman
title: Nurse of the Prophet
bio: Barakah, who cared for the Prophet ﷺ as a child and remained close to his family. She migrated to Medina and was among the early believers.

name: Al-Khansa
title: The Poetess
bio: A famous Arab poetess known for her elegies. She accepted Islam and encouraged her sons to fight at al-Qadisiyyah, where they were martyred.

name: Rufayda al-Aslamiyya
title: The First Muslim Nurse
bio: A woman of Medina who treated the wounded in a tent near the mosque during the battles of Badr, Uhud and the Trench. She is often called the first nurse in Islam.

name: Umm Haram bint Milhan
title: Sailor in the Way of Allah
bio: A woman of the Ansar, aunt of Anas, who accompanied the first Muslim naval expedition to Cyprus and died there.

name: Asma bint Yazid
title: Speaker of the Women
bio: A woman of the Ansar famed for her eloquence, who spoke to the Prophet ﷺ on behalf of the women of Medina. She is also said to have fought at Yarmouk.

name: Fatima bint al-Khattab
title: Sister of Umar
bio: The sister of Umar and wife of Sa'id ibn Zayd. She accepted Islam early, and her recitation of the Quran deeply moved her brother Umar before he became Muslim.

name: Umm Waraqa bint Abdullah
title: Memorizer of the Quran
bio: A woman of Medina who learned the Quran and was allowed by the Prophet ﷺ to lead the women of her household in prayer.

name: Al-Hasan al-Basri
title: Preacher of Basra
bio: A leading Tabi'i of Basra (d. 110 AH) who met many companions. He was famous for his powerful sermons, his asceticism and his knowledge.

name: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib
title: Master of the Tabi'un
bio: A scholar of Medina (d. around 94 AH) who learned from many companions. He is counted among the seven great jurists of Medina and was admired for his firmness.

name: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz
title: The Just Caliph
bio: The Umayyad caliph (d. 101 AH) who ruled for about two and a half years. He was known for justice, simple living and for ordering the recording of hadith.

name: Muhammad ibn Sirin
title: Scrupulous Narrator of Basra
bio: A Tabi'i of Basra (d. 110 AH) known for his piety and care in narrating. He insisted that people ask for the chain of narrators of a report.

name: Urwa ibn az-Zubayr
title: Nephew of Aisha
bio: One of the seven great jurists of Medina. He learned from his aunt Aisha and passed on many of her narrations and accounts of the Prophet's life.

name: Ibn Shihab az-Zuhri
title: Early Compiler of Hadith
bio: A scholar of Medina (d. 124 AH) who was asked by Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz to collect hadith in writing. He was a main source for the later hadith collections.

name: Nafi' Mawla Ibn Umar
title: Narrator from Ibn Umar
bio: A freed servant of Abdullah ibn Umar who learned from him for many years. His narrations through Ibn Umar are considered among the most reliable chains.

name: Mujahid ibn Jabr
title: Student of Ibn Abbas
bio: A leading early interpreter of the Quran (d. around 104 AH) who read the whole Quran to Ibn Abbas several times, stopping at every verse to ask about it.

name: Ata ibn Abi Rabah
title: Mufti of Mecca
bio: A Tabi'i (d. around 114 AH) who became the main teacher and mufti in Mecca. He was known for knowing the rites of Hajj better than anyone.

name: Tawus ibn Kaysan
title: Scholar of Yemen
bio: A Tabi'i from Yemen who learned from many companions and was known for his devotion and courage in speaking the truth to rulers.

name: Qatada ibn Di'ama
title: The Blind Memorizer
bio: A blind Tabi'i of Basra (d. around 117 AH) with an exceptional memory. He was a respected interpreter of the Quran and narrator of hadith.

name: Alqama ibn Qays
title: Student of Ibn Mas'ud
bio: A Tabi'i of Kufa who learned from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud and carried his knowledge to the next generation. He was a source for the Kufan school of fiqh.

name: Sa'id ibn Jubayr
title: Martyr of Truth
bio: A student of Ibn Abbas who became a leading scholar of Kufa. He was executed by al-Hajjaj in 95 AH after refusing to give up what he believed was right.

name: Ali ibn al-Husayn Zayn al-Abidin
title: The Devout of Medina
bio: The son of al-Husayn and a respected Tabi'i of Medina, admired for his worship and knowledge. He narrated hadith and taught in the city.

name: Abu Yusuf
title: Chief Judge of Harun ar-Rashid
bio: The chief student of Abu Hanifa (d. 182 AH) and the first chief judge of the Abbasid state. He wrote Kitab al-Kharaj on taxation and public finance.

name: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ash-Shaybani
title: Student of Abu Hanifa
bio: A student of Abu Hanifa and Abu Yusuf (d. 189 AH) who wrote down and organized the Hanafi school. He also studied with Malik in Medina.

name: Al-Layth ibn Sa'd
title: Imam of Egypt
bio: A leading jurist and hadith scholar of Egypt (d. 175 AH), famed for his generosity. Ash-Shafi'i said he was a better jurist than Malik, but his students did not preserve his school.

name: Sufyan ibn Uyayna
title: Hadith Scholar of Mecca
bio: A scholar of Mecca (d. 198 AH) who taught many famous students, including ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad. He was an authority on the hadith of the Hijaz.

name: Waki' ibn al-Jarrah
title: Teacher of Imam Ahmad
bio: A scholar of Kufa (d. 197 AH) known for his strong memory and devotion. He was a teacher of ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad ibn Hanbal.

name: Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan
title: Founder of Hadith Criticism
bio: A scholar of Basra (d. 198 AH) regarded as a founder of the science of evaluating narrators, which later hadith critics built upon.

name: Ali ibn al-Madini
title: Teacher of al-Bukhari
bio: A leading hadith critic (d. 234 AH) and teacher of al-Bukhari. He was an authority on the identification of narrators and the defects hidden in chains.

name: Yahya ibn Ma'in
title: Critic of Narrators
bio: A famous hadith critic of Baghdad (d. 233 AH) and a close companion of Ahmad ibn Hanbal. His judgments on narrators are quoted throughout the books of rijal.

name: Ishaq ibn Rahawayh
title: Scholar of Khurasan
bio: A scholar of Nishapur (d. 238 AH) who traveled widely in seeking knowledge. He was a companion of Ahmad and a teacher of al-Bukhari and Muslim.

name: Ibn Abi Shayba
title: Author of al-Musannaf
bio: A hadith scholar of Kufa (d. 235 AH) who compiled al-Musannaf, a huge collection of hadith and the sayings of the companions and Tabi'un.

name: Abd ar-Razzaq as-San'ani
title: Scholar of Yemen
bio: A hadith scholar of San'a (d. 211 AH) and author of a large Musannaf. Many famous scholars traveled to Yemen to learn from him.

name: Ad-Darimi
title: Author of the Sunan
bio: A scholar of Samarkand (d. 255 AH) who compiled the Musnad known as Sunan ad-Darimi. He also served as a judge.

name: Al-Fudayl ibn Iyad
title: The Devoted Worshipper
bio: A scholar and ascetic who lived in Mecca (d. 187 AH). In his youth he was a highway robber, then repented and became known for his piety and sincerity.

name: Sahnun
title: Judge of Kairouan
bio: A leading Maliki scholar of Kairouan (d. 240 AH) and author of al-Mudawwana. His work spread the Maliki school across North Africa.

name: Asad ibn al-Furat
title: Scholar Who Led the Conquest of Sicily
bio: A scholar and judge of Kairouan who led the Aghlabid expedition that landed in Sicily in 827 CE. He died during the siege of Syracuse.

name: Ibn Abi Zayd al-Qayrawani
title: Author of ar-Risala
bio: A Maliki scholar of Kairouan (d. 386 AH) whose Risala, a concise book of creed and fiqh, was memorized by students across the Maghreb.

name: Ibn Hazm
title: Zahiri Scholar of Cordoba
bio: A scholar of Al-Andalus (d. 456 AH) who followed the literal Zahiri school. He wrote al-Muhalla on fiqh, and a famous work on the comparison of religions.

name: Qadi Iyad
title: Judge of Ceuta
bio: A Maliki scholar and judge from Ceuta (d. 544 AH), author of ash-Shifa, a well-known book on the status and character of the Prophet ﷺ.

name: Ash-Shatibi
title: Author of al-Muwafaqat
bio: An Andalusian Maliki scholar (d. 790 AH) who wrote al-Muwafaqat, a major work on the objectives of Islamic law, and al-I'tisam.

name: Imam at-Tabari
title: Master of Tafsir and History
bio: A scholar of Baghdad (d. 310 AH) who wrote Jami' al-Bayan, one of the most important commentaries on the Quran, and a great universal history of the world and the Muslims.

name: Ibn Khuzayma
title: Imam of Nishapur
bio: A hadith scholar (d. 311 AH) known as the Imam of the Imams. He compiled a Sahih collection and wrote Kitab at-Tawhid.

name: Ibn Hibban
title: Author of the Sahih
bio: A hadith scholar and judge from Bust (d. 354 AH) who compiled a large Sahih collection and works on narrators.

name: At-Tabarani
title: Master of the Mu'jams
bio: A hadith scholar (d. 360 AH) who collected a very large number of narrations in his three Mu'jams, traveling widely to find them.

name: Al-Ajurri
title: Author of ash-Shari'a
bio: A scholar who settled in Mecca (d. 360 AH). His book ash-Shari'a is a classic on the creed of the Salaf, and he also wrote on the ethics of the scholars.

name: Al-Barbahari
title: Leader of the Hanbalis in Baghdad
bio: A Hanbali scholar of Baghdad (d. 329 AH) whose Sharh as-Sunnah is a short and influential statement of the creed of Ahl as-Sunnah.

name: Ad-Daraqutni
title: Critic of Hadith
bio: A hadith scholar of Baghdad (d. 385 AH) famous for his Sunan and his books pointing out hidden defects in narrations.

name: Al-Hakim an-Naysaburi
title: Author of al-Mustadrak
bio: A hadith scholar of Nishapur (d. 405 AH) who compiled al-Mustadrak, a large collection that adds narrations on the conditions of the two Sahihs.

name: Abu Nu'aym al-Isfahani
title: Author of Hilyat al-Awliya
bio: A hadith scholar of Isfahan (d. 430 AH) who wrote Hilyat al-Awliya, a biographical work on the pious from the companions onward.

name: Al-Bayhaqi
title: Author of as-Sunan al-Kubra
bio: A hadith scholar and jurist (d. 458 AH) who wrote as-Sunan al-Kubra and other major works linking hadith to the rulings of the schools.

name: Al-Khatib al-Baghdadi
title: Historian of Baghdad
bio: A hadith scholar (d. 463 AH) who wrote the history of Baghdad and important books on the science of hadith.

name: Ibn Asakir
title: Historian of Damascus
bio: A hadith scholar of Damascus (d. 571 AH) who wrote Tarikh Dimashq, a huge biographical history of the city and its people.

name: Ibn al-Jawzi
title: The Preacher of Baghdad
bio: A Hanbali scholar and preacher (d. 597 AH) who wrote on a huge range of subjects, from history and hadith to exhortation and Quranic studies.

name: Ibn as-Salah
title: Author of the Muqaddimah
bio: A Shafi'i hadith scholar (d. 643 AH) whose Muqaddimah on the sciences of hadith became the standard reference for later scholars.

name: An-Nawawi
title: Author of Riyad as-Salihin
bio: A Shafi'i scholar of Damascus (d. 676 AH) who wrote Riyad as-Salihin, the Forty Hadith and a commentary on Sahih Muslim. He lived simply and died in his forties.

name: Al-Qurtubi
title: Mufassir of Al-Andalus
bio: A Maliki scholar from Cordoba who settled in Egypt (d. 671 AH). His commentary on the Quran, al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran, focuses on legal rulings.

name: Al-Baghawi
title: Author of Ma'alim at-Tanzil
bio: A Shafi'i scholar of Khurasan (d. around 516 AH) who wrote a widely used commentary on the Quran based on narrations, and Sharh as-Sunnah.

name: Al-Mizzi
title: Author of Tahdhib al-Kamal
bio: A hadith scholar of Damascus (d. 742 AH) who wrote Tahdhib al-Kamal, a large dictionary of the narrators of the six books. Adh-Dhahabi was among his students.

name: As-Suyuti
title: The Prolific Author
bio: An Egyptian scholar (d. 911 AH) who wrote hundreds of works on the Quran, hadith, history, language and fiqh, including a famous continuation of the commentary of al-Mahalli.

name: Ash-Shawkani
title: Scholar of Yemen
bio: A Yemeni scholar (d. 1250 AH) who served as a judge and wrote Fath al-Qadir, a commentary on the Quran, and Nayl al-Awtar on hadith.

name: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab
title: Reformer of Najd
bio: A scholar of Najd (d. 1206 AH) who called for a return to pure tawhid. His alliance with Muhammad ibn Saud in 1744 led to the first Saudi state.

name: Abd ar-Rahman as-Sa'di
title: Mufassir of Unayzah
bio: A scholar of Unayzah in Najd (d. 1376 AH) known for his clear and simple commentary on the Quran, Taysir al-Karim ar-Rahman, and his teaching of many students.

name: Muhammad al-Amin ash-Shanqiti
title: Scholar of Shinqit
bio: A scholar from Mauritania (d. 1393 AH) who taught in Medina and wrote Adwa' al-Bayan, a commentary that explains the Quran with the Quran.

name: Ahmad Shakir
title: Editor of the Musnad
bio: An Egyptian hadith scholar (d. 1377 AH) who edited the Musnad of Ahmad and the Risala of ash-Shafi'i and wrote on the verification of hadith.

name: Muqbil al-Wadi'i
title: Scholar of Dammaj
bio: A Yemeni hadith scholar (d. 1422 AH) who founded Dar al-Hadith in Dammaj and taught students from many countries.

name: Abdelhamid Ben Badis
title: Reviver of Algeria
bio: An Algerian scholar of Constantine (d. 1940) who founded the Association of Algerian Muslim Scholars in 1931 and worked to renew religion, language and education under French rule.

name: Bachir al-Ibrahimi
title: Successor of Ben Badis
bio: An Algerian scholar and writer (d. 1965) who led the Association of Algerian Muslim Scholars after Ben Badis and defended the Arabic language and Islam in Algeria.

name: Mu'awiya ibn Abi Sufyan
title: Founder of the Umayyad Caliphate
bio: A companion and scribe of the Prophet ﷺ who governed Syria for two decades. He became caliph in 661 CE, founded the Umayyad dynasty and built the first Muslim navy.

name: Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan
title: The Consolidator
bio: The Umayyad caliph (d. 705 CE) who restored the unity of the state, made Arabic the language of administration, introduced Islamic coinage and built the Dome of the Rock.

name: Al-Walid ibn Abd al-Malik
title: Caliph of the Great Expansion
bio: The Umayyad caliph (d. 715 CE) in whose reign the Muslim armies reached Transoxiana, Sindh and Al-Andalus. He built the Great Mosque of Damascus.

name: Qutayba ibn Muslim
title: Conqueror of Transoxiana
bio: An Umayyad general who led the conquest of Bukhara, Samarkand and other lands beyond the Oxus river in the early 8th century, and was killed in 715 CE.

name: Maslama ibn Abd al-Malik
title: Commander at Constantinople
bio: An Umayyad prince and general who led the great siege of Constantinople in 717-718 CE and fought many campaigns against the Byzantines.

name: Hassan ibn an-Nu'man
title: Conqueror of Carthage
bio: An Umayyad governor of North Africa who captured Carthage in 698 CE and ended Byzantine rule in the region.

name: Abd ar-Rahman I ad-Dakhil
title: Falcon of Quraysh
bio: A survivor of the Umayyad family who escaped the Abbasid takeover, crossed into Al-Andalus and founded the Emirate of Cordoba in 756 CE.

name: Abd ar-Rahman III
title: First Caliph of Cordoba
bio: The ruler of Al-Andalus (d. 961 CE) who declared the Caliphate of Cordoba in 929 CE and led it to its peak of power and culture.

name: Al-Mansur
title: Founder of Baghdad
bio: The second Abbasid caliph (d. 775 CE) who founded the round city of Baghdad in 762 CE and secured the new dynasty.

name: Harun ar-Rashid
title: Caliph of the Golden Age
bio: The Abbasid caliph (d. 809 CE) whose reign saw Baghdad at its height as a center of knowledge, trade and power.

name: Al-Ma'mun
title: Patron of the House of Wisdom
bio: The Abbasid caliph (d. 833 CE) who supported the translation movement and the House of Wisdom. He also imposed the doctrine of the created Quran, which Imam Ahmad refused.

name: Al-Mu'tasim
title: Conqueror of Amorium
bio: The Abbasid caliph (d. 842 CE) who captured the Byzantine city of Amorium in 838 CE after a famous campaign.

name: Ahmad ibn Tulun
title: Founder of the Tulunids
bio: A Turkish governor of Egypt who made the country largely independent in 868 CE. He built the Mosque of Ibn Tulun in Cairo, which still stands.

name: Al-Mansur ibn Abi Amir
title: Almanzor of Al-Andalus
bio: The chief minister and real ruler of Al-Andalus (d. 1002 CE), who led more than fifty campaigns and was said never to have lost a battle.

name: Abd ar-Rahman al-Ghafiqi
title: Governor of Al-Andalus
bio: The governor of Al-Andalus who led a large army north into Gaul and was killed in the battle between Tours and Poitiers in 732 CE.

name: Alp Arslan
title: Victor of Manzikert
bio: The Seljuk sultan (d. 1072 CE) who defeated the Byzantine emperor at Manzikert in 1071 CE, opening Anatolia to the Turks.

name: Malik-Shah I
title: Sultan of the Seljuk Empire
bio: The Seljuk sultan (d. 1092 CE) under whom the empire reached its peak, supported by his vizier Nizam al-Mulk.

name: Nizam al-Mulk
title: Vizier of the Seljuks
bio: The Seljuk vizier (d. 1092 CE) who ran the empire for decades and founded the Nizamiyya schools in major cities.

name: Mahmud of Ghazni
title: Sultan of the Ghaznavids
bio: The Ghaznavid ruler (d. 1030 CE) who built a large empire from Afghanistan into India and made Ghazni a center of learning and the arts.

name: Abd al-Mu'min
title: First Almohad Caliph
bio: The first Almohad caliph (d. 1163 CE), who took Marrakesh in 1147 CE and united North Africa and much of Al-Andalus under one state.

name: Ya'qub al-Mansur
title: Victor of Alarcos
bio: The Almohad caliph (d. 1199 CE) who defeated the army of Alfonso VIII of Castile at Alarcos in 1195 CE.

name: Imad ad-Din Zangi
title: Conqueror of Edessa
bio: The ruler of Mosul and Aleppo (d. 1146 CE) who recaptured Edessa from the Crusaders in 1144 CE, and the father of Nur ad-Din.

name: Asad ad-Din Shirkuh
title: Uncle of Salah ad-Din
bio: A Kurdish commander in the service of Nur ad-Din (d. 1169 CE) who led campaigns in Egypt and became its vizier shortly before his death.

name: Shajar ad-Durr
title: Sultana of Egypt
bio: The widow of the Ayyubid sultan as-Salih Ayyub who helped to rally Egypt during the Crusade of Louis IX and ruled briefly in 1250 CE.

name: Qalawun
title: Mamluk Sultan
bio: The Mamluk sultan (d. 1290 CE) who took Tripoli from the Crusaders in 1289 CE and built a famous hospital and school complex in Cairo.

name: Al-Ashraf Khalil
title: Conqueror of Acre
bio: The Mamluk sultan (d. 1293 CE) who captured Acre in 1291 CE, ending the Crusader presence on the mainland of the Levant.

name: Osman I
title: Founder of the Ottoman State
bio: The leader of a small Turkish principality in Anatolia (d. around 1324 CE) whose family went on to build the Ottoman Empire.

name: Orhan Ghazi
title: Second Ottoman Ruler
bio: The son of Osman (d. 1362 CE) who captured Bursa in 1326 CE, made it the Ottoman capital and began the expansion into Europe.

name: Murad I
title: Sultan of the Balkans
bio: The Ottoman sultan who conquered Adrianople and much of the Balkans and was killed at the Battle of Kosovo in 1389 CE.

name: Bayezid I
title: The Thunderbolt
bio: The Ottoman sultan who won the Battle of Nicopolis in 1396 CE and was defeated by Timur at Ankara in 1402 CE.

name: Selim I
title: Conqueror of the Mamluks
bio: The Ottoman sultan (d. 1520 CE) who defeated the Mamluks in 1516-1517 CE and added Syria, Egypt and the holy cities of Mecca and Medina to the empire.

name: Suleiman the Magnificent
title: The Lawgiver
bio: The Ottoman sultan (d. 1566 CE) under whom the empire reached its greatest power. He is also remembered for his legal reforms and for the buildings of Sinan.

name: Hayreddin Barbarossa
title: Admiral of Algiers
bio: A naval commander who made Algiers an Ottoman province and a base of power in the Mediterranean. He won the Battle of Preveza in 1538 CE and died in 1546 CE.

name: Oruc Reis
title: Corsair of Algiers
bio: The elder brother of Hayreddin who took Algiers in 1516 CE and was killed in 1518 CE while fighting near Tlemcen.

name: Turgut Reis
title: Admiral of the Ottoman Navy
bio: A celebrated Ottoman admiral and governor of Tripoli who was killed at the siege of Malta in 1565 CE.

name: Ahmed Bey of Constantine
title: Defender of Constantine
bio: The last Bey of Constantine, who resisted the French conquest after the fall of his city in 1837 CE and kept fighting in the Aures until 1848 CE.

name: Lalla Fatma n'Soumer
title: Heroine of Kabylia
bio: A Kabyle woman who led resistance against the French conquest of Kabylia in the 1850s. She was captured in 1857 CE and died in 1863 CE.

name: Imam Shamil
title: Leader of the Caucasus
bio: The imam of Dagestan and Chechnya who led the resistance against the Russian conquest of the Caucasus for 25 years until his surrender in 1859 CE.

name: Abd el-Krim al-Khattabi
title: Leader of the Rif
bio: A Moroccan scholar and leader who defeated a Spanish army at Annual in 1921 CE and founded the Republic of the Rif, which fell in 1926 CE.

name: Usman dan Fodio
title: Founder of the Sokoto Caliphate
bio: A scholar and reformer of West Africa (d. 1817 CE) who led a movement of reform in Hausaland and founded the Sokoto Caliphate in 1804 CE.

name: Askia Muhammad
title: Emperor of Songhai
bio: The ruler of the Songhai Empire (d. 1538 CE) who made the pilgrimage to Mecca in 1496-1497 CE and strengthened Islamic scholarship in Timbuktu.

name: Mansa Musa
title: Emperor of Mali
bio: The ruler of the Mali Empire (d. around 1337 CE) whose pilgrimage to Mecca in 1324 CE became famous across the Muslim world for the gold he distributed on the way.

name: Tipu Sultan
title: Tiger of Mysore
bio: The ruler of Mysore in southern India who fought the British East India Company and was killed defending his capital Seringapatam in 1799 CE.

name: The Constitution of Medina
title: The First Charter of the City
bio: After the Hijrah the Prophet ﷺ set out an agreement between the Muslims and the other communities of Medina, defining rights, duties and mutual defense in the city.

name: The Building of Quba Mosque
title: The First Mosque of Islam
bio: On reaching Quba, just outside Medina, in 622 CE, the Prophet ﷺ helped to build the first mosque of Islam, which the Quran says was founded on piety.

name: The Change of the Qibla
title: Turning Toward the Kaaba
bio: In 2 AH, while the Muslims were praying in Medina, the direction of prayer was changed from Jerusalem to the Kaaba in Mecca.

name: The Obligation of Fasting
title: The Month of Ramadan
bio: In 2 AH fasting in the month of Ramadan became obligatory on the Muslims, the same year as the Battle of Badr and the change of the qibla.

name: The Expulsion of Banu Qaynuqa
title: The First Jewish Tribe to Break the Pact
bio: After the Battle of Badr, the Jewish tribe of Banu Qaynuqa broke the agreement of Medina by attacking a Muslim woman, and was sent out of the city.

name: The Expulsion of Banu Nadir
title: The Plot Against the Prophet
bio: In 4 AH the Muslims besieged the tribe of Banu Nadir after they plotted against the Prophet ﷺ, and the tribe left Medina. Surah al-Hashr speaks about it.

name: The Expedition of Banu al-Mustaliq
title: The Campaign of al-Muraysi
bio: In 5 or 6 AH the Muslims marched against the tribe of Banu al-Mustaliq, who were preparing to attack. Juwayriyya later became a wife of the Prophet ﷺ.

name: The Pledge of Ridwan
title: The Pledge Under the Tree
bio: At Hudaybiyyah in 6 AH, about fourteen hundred companions pledged loyalty to the Prophet ﷺ under a tree when news came that Uthman might have been killed. Allah praised them in the Quran.

name: The Letters to the Kings
title: The Call Beyond Arabia
bio: After Hudaybiyyah the Prophet ﷺ sent letters inviting rulers such as Heraclius, Khosrow, the Negus and the ruler of Egypt to Islam.

name: The Fulfilled Umrah
title: Return to Mecca
bio: In 7 AH, in line with the treaty of Hudaybiyyah, the Muslims entered Mecca for the first time since the Hijrah to perform Umrah, and stayed three days.

name: Expedition of Dhat as-Salasil
title: The Campaign of Amr
bio: In 8 AH Amr ibn al-As led an expedition toward the north. He asked for reinforcements, and Abu Ubayda was sent to help him.

name: The Siege of Ta'if
title: Return From the Hawazin Campaign
bio: After Hunayn in 8 AH the Muslims besieged the fortified town of Ta'if. The Prophet ﷺ withdrew and prayed for its people, who accepted Islam the next year.

name: The Year of Delegations
title: Tribes Come to Medina
bio: In 9 AH delegations from tribes across Arabia came to Medina to accept Islam, after the conquest of Mecca had changed the balance of power.

name: The Passing of the Prophet
title: The Day Medina Fell Silent
bio: In Rabi' al-Awwal 11 AH the Prophet ﷺ passed away in Medina in the room of Aisha. Abu Bakr reminded the grieving Muslims that Allah is ever-living.

name: The Gathering of Saqifa
title: Choosing the First Caliph
bio: After the Prophet's passing, the Ansar and the Muhajirun met at Saqifa Bani Sa'ida, and Abu Bakr was chosen as the first caliph.

name: The Ridda Wars
title: Holding the Ummah Together
bio: Under Abu Bakr, the Muslims fought tribes that refused to pay zakat or followed false prophets, and brought all of Arabia back under one state in 632-633 CE.

name: The Compilation of the Quran
title: From Memory to a Book
bio: After Yamama, Abu Bakr had Zayd ibn Thabit gather the Quran into one written copy. Under Uthman, copies were made and sent to the main cities.

name: Battle of Ajnadayn
title: The Opening of Palestine
bio: Fought in 634 CE between the Muslim armies and the Byzantines in Palestine. The Muslim victory opened the way to the conquest of the Levant.

name: Battle of Fahl
title: Victory in the Jordan Valley
bio: A Muslim victory over the Byzantines in the Jordan valley around 635 CE, which helped to secure the way to Damascus.

name: The Conquest of Damascus
title: City of the Umayyads
bio: In 635 CE Damascus surrendered to the Muslim army under Khalid ibn al-Walid and Abu Ubayda after a siege, and later became the capital of the Umayyads.

name: The Conquest of Jerusalem
title: Umar Enters Jerusalem
bio: Around 637 CE the people of Jerusalem agreed to a treaty with the Muslims and asked that the caliph Umar come to receive the city. He granted them security for their lives and churches.

name: Battle of Nahavand
title: The Victory of Victories
bio: Fought around 642 CE in Persia against the last major Sasanian army. The Muslim victory sealed the fall of the Persian empire.

name: The Conquest of Egypt
title: Amr Enters the Land of the Nile
bio: Amr ibn al-As led the Muslim army into Egypt around 640 CE and took Babylon and then Alexandria, where the city was handed over by treaty in the following years.

name: The Founding of Fustat
title: First Muslim City in Egypt
bio: After the conquest of Egypt, Amr ibn al-As founded Fustat around 641 CE with its mosque, which became the first Islamic capital of Egypt.

name: The Founding of Basra and Kufa
title: The Garrison Cities of Iraq
bio: In the time of Umar the Muslims founded the garrison cities of Basra and Kufa in Iraq, which soon became great centers of learning.

name: The First Siege of Constantinople
title: The Umayyad Naval Campaign
bio: In the 670s CE the Umayyad navy and army besieged Constantinople for several years under Mu'awiya, but failed to take the city. Abu Ayyub al-Ansari died during this campaign.

name: The Battle of Karbala
title: The Martyrdom of al-Husayn
bio: In 61 AH (680 CE) al-Husayn, grandson of the Prophet ﷺ, was killed with his family and companions at Karbala by the army of the governor of Kufa, a day remembered with deep sorrow.

name: The Battle of Tahouda
title: The Death of Uqba
bio: In 683 CE near Biskra in what is now Algeria, the army of Uqba ibn Nafi was ambushed by Berber forces under Kusayla and Uqba was killed on the way back from the Atlantic.

name: The Building of the Dome of the Rock
title: The Jewel of Jerusalem
bio: Completed in 691-692 CE under Abd al-Malik, the Dome of the Rock on the Haram in Jerusalem is the oldest great monument of Islamic architecture.

name: The Building of the Umayyad Mosque
title: The Great Mosque of Damascus
bio: Built under al-Walid I between 705 and 715 CE on the site of an older church, the Great Mosque of Damascus became a model for later mosques.

name: The Battle of Talas
title: Meeting of Two Empires
bio: In 751 CE an Abbasid army met a Chinese Tang army by the Talas river in Central Asia. The Abbasid victory secured the region, and papermaking later spread westward.

name: The Founding of Baghdad
title: The Round City
bio: In 762 CE the caliph al-Mansur founded Baghdad on the Tigris as the capital of the Abbasids. It grew into one of the largest and most learned cities in the world.

name: The Emirate of Cordoba
title: The Umayyads of Al-Andalus
bio: In 756 CE Abd ar-Rahman I took Cordoba and founded the Umayyad emirate in Al-Andalus, which later became a caliphate and a center of science.

name: The House of Wisdom
title: The Translation Movement
bio: In Abbasid Baghdad, especially under al-Ma'mun, scholars translated and built upon the works of the Greeks, Persians and Indians, and added much of their own.

name: The Trial of Imam Ahmad
title: Steadfast Under the Whip
bio: In the time of al-Ma'mun and his successors the state forced scholars to say the Quran was created. Ahmad ibn Hanbal refused, was imprisoned and beaten, and his steadfastness became a landmark.

name: The Sack of Amorium
title: The Call of Al-Mu'tasim
bio: In 838 CE the Abbasid caliph al-Mu'tasim led an army to Amorium in Anatolia and captured it. The poet Abu Tammam celebrated the victory in a famous poem.

name: The Conquest of Sicily
title: Landing at Mazara
bio: In 827 CE an expedition from Kairouan under Asad ibn al-Furat landed in Sicily. The conquest took decades and the island became a center of Muslim culture.

name: The Founding of Cairo
title: The City Victorious
bio: In 969 CE the Fatimid general Jawhar founded Cairo, near the old Fustat. The city soon grew into a major capital of the Muslim world.

name: The Battle of Manzikert
title: The Gate to Anatolia
bio: In 1071 CE the Seljuk sultan Alp Arslan defeated and captured the Byzantine emperor Romanos IV, opening Anatolia to Turkish settlement.

name: The Fall of Jerusalem in 1099
title: The Crusader Conquest
bio: In 1099 CE the Crusaders took Jerusalem after a siege and killed many of its people. The city stayed under Crusader rule for 88 years until Salah ad-Din retook it.

name: The Battle of Alarcos
title: Almohad Victory
bio: In 1195 CE the Almohad caliph Ya'qub al-Mansur defeated the army of Alfonso VIII of Castile at Alarcos in central Spain.

name: The Battle of Las Navas de Tolosa
title: The Turning Point in Spain
bio: In 1212 CE a coalition of Christian kingdoms defeated the Almohad army at Las Navas de Tolosa. The battle marked the start of the decline of Muslim power in Al-Andalus.

name: The Fall of Baghdad
title: The Mongol Siege
bio: In 1258 CE the Mongols under Hulagu besieged and took Baghdad, ended the Abbasid caliphate there and destroyed much of the city and its libraries.

name: The Battle of al-Mansoura
title: The Defeat of the Seventh Crusade
bio: In 1250 CE the Muslim forces in Egypt defeated the army of Louis IX of France at al-Mansoura and captured the king.

name: The Fall of Acre
title: The End of the Crusader States
bio: In 1291 CE the Mamluk sultan al-Ashraf Khalil took Acre, the last major Crusader stronghold in the Levant.

name: The Fall of Granada
title: End of Muslim Spain
bio: In January 1492 CE Granada surrendered to the Catholic monarchs, ending almost eight centuries of Muslim rule in Al-Andalus. Many Muslims were later forced to convert or leave.

name: The Battle of Preveza
title: Ottoman Mastery of the Sea
bio: In 1538 CE the Ottoman fleet under Hayreddin Barbarossa defeated a Christian alliance off the Greek coast, giving the Ottomans control of the Mediterranean for decades.

name: The Battle of Mohacs
title: The Fall of Hungary
bio: In 1526 CE Suleiman the Magnificent defeated the Hungarian army at Mohacs, which opened Hungary to Ottoman rule.

name: The Siege of Vienna
title: High Tide of the Ottomans
bio: In 1683 CE a large Ottoman army besieged Vienna and was defeated by a relief force. The battle began the slow retreat of the Ottomans from Central Europe.

name: The French Invasion of Algiers
title: The Start of the Colonial Era
bio: In July 1830 CE a French expeditionary force landed near Algiers and took the city. The conquest of Algeria that followed lasted decades and met strong resistance.

name: The Algerian Revolution
title: The Day of 1 November
bio: On 1 November 1954 the National Liberation Front launched the war of independence against French rule. After eight years of struggle Algeria became independent on 5 July 1962.

name: Al-Khwarizmi
title: Father of Algebra
bio: A scholar of the House of Wisdom in Baghdad (d. around 850 CE) whose book on al-jabr gave algebra its name. His name is also the origin of the word algorithm.

name: Ibn al-Haytham
title: Father of Optics
bio: A scholar who worked in Cairo (d. around 1040 CE) and wrote the Book of Optics. He tested ideas about vision and light by experiment.

name: Ibn Sina
title: The Physician of the East
bio: A physician and philosopher (d. 1037 CE) from Central Asia. His Canon of Medicine was used as a medical textbook in the Muslim world and in Europe for centuries.

name: Al-Razi
title: Physician of Rayy
bio: A physician and chemist (d. around 925 CE) who wrote a large medical encyclopedia and one of the first clear treatises distinguishing smallpox from measles.

name: Az-Zahrawi
title: Master Surgeon of Cordoba
bio: A physician at the court of Cordoba (d. around 1013 CE) whose encyclopedia at-Tasrif described many surgical instruments and techniques.

name: Al-Biruni
title: The Polymath
bio: A scholar from Central Asia (d. around 1050 CE) who wrote on astronomy, geography, mathematics and India. He calculated the radius of the earth with remarkable accuracy.

name: Ibn Khaldun
title: Father of Sociology
bio: A historian and judge (d. 1406 CE) born in Tunis. He wrote the Muqaddimah, a groundbreaking study of history and society, while living in what is now Algeria.

name: Ibn Battuta
title: The Great Traveler
bio: A scholar from Tangier (d. around 1369 CE) who traveled more than a hundred thousand kilometers across Africa, Asia and Europe and described his journeys in the Rihla.

name: Al-Idrisi
title: Mapmaker of Sicily
bio: A geographer from Ceuta (d. around 1165 CE) who produced a famous world map and atlas for King Roger II of Sicily in 1154 CE.

name: Ibn Rushd
title: Judge of Cordoba
bio: A judge, physician and philosopher of Al-Andalus (d. 1198 CE). He wrote on medicine and philosophy, and Bidayat al-Mujtahid, a book comparing the opinions of the jurists.

name: Al-Jazari
title: Engineer of Mechanical Wonders
bio: An engineer at the court of Diyarbakir (d. 1206 CE) who wrote a book describing about fifty machines, including water clocks, pumps and automata.

name: Ibn al-Nafis
title: Physician of Cairo
bio: A physician of Damascus and Cairo (d. 1288 CE) who described the passage of blood through the lungs, centuries before it was accepted in Europe.

name: Al-Kindi
title: Philosopher of the Arabs
bio: A scholar of Baghdad (d. around 873 CE) who wrote on mathematics, medicine and philosophy and described the method of frequency analysis for breaking codes.

name: Al-Farabi
title: The Second Teacher
bio: A philosopher and music theorist (d. 950 CE) born in Central Asia who wrote widely on logic, politics and music.

name: The Banu Musa
title: The Three Brothers of Baghdad
bio: Three brothers of the 9th century CE who worked for the Abbasid caliphs and wrote the Book of Ingenious Devices, an early work on mechanics.

name: Al-Battani
title: Astronomer of Raqqa
bio: An astronomer and mathematician (d. 929 CE) who measured the length of the solar year with great accuracy and improved the use of trigonometry.

name: Omar Khayyam
title: Mathematician and Poet
bio: A scholar of Nishapur (d. 1131 CE) who solved cubic equations and helped create the Jalali calendar, a very accurate solar calendar. He is also known for his quatrains.

name: Nasir ad-Din at-Tusi
title: Founder of Maragha Observatory
bio: A scholar (d. 1274 CE) who led the observatory of Maragha and developed astronomical models that influenced later astronomers.

name: Ulugh Beg
title: Astronomer-Prince of Samarkand
bio: A ruler and astronomer (d. 1449 CE) who built a large observatory in Samarkand and produced a star catalogue that remained a reference for centuries.

name: Abbas ibn Firnas
title: Dreamer of Flight
bio: A polymath of Al-Andalus (d. 887 CE) known for his inventions and for an attempt to fly with a self-made glider near Cordoba.

name: Fatima al-Fihri
title: Founder of al-Qarawiyyin
bio: A woman of Fez who used her inheritance to found the Qarawiyyin Mosque and school in 859 CE, which grew into one of the oldest continuously running centers of learning.

name: Piri Reis
title: Cartographer of the Ottoman Fleet
bio: An Ottoman admiral and mapmaker (d. around 1553 CE) who drew a famous world map in 1513 CE and wrote a detailed book of sailing directions.

name: Zheng He
title: Admiral of the Treasure Fleets
bio: A Chinese Muslim admiral (d. around 1433 CE) who led seven great naval expeditions from 1405 to 1433 CE across the Indian Ocean as far as Arabia and East Africa.

name: Ahmad ibn Majid
title: Navigator of the Indian Ocean
bio: An Arab navigator (d. after 1500 CE) who wrote detailed pilot books on the seas between Arabia, India and East Africa.

name: Ibn Jubayr
title: Traveler from Valencia
bio: A traveler from Al-Andalus (d. 1217 CE) who made the pilgrimage to Mecca and described the lands and cities he saw in his Rihla.

name: Al-Mas'udi
title: Historian and Geographer
bio: A historian from Baghdad (d. 956 CE) who traveled widely and wrote Muruj adh-Dhahab, a history that mixes events with geography and customs of many peoples.

name: Ahmad ibn Fadlan
title: Envoy to the Volga
bio: An envoy sent by the Abbasid caliph in 921 CE to the king of the Volga Bulgars, who wrote a valuable account of the peoples he met on the way.

name: Mimar Sinan
title: The Great Ottoman Architect
bio: The chief architect of the Ottoman sultans (d. 1588 CE) who designed hundreds of buildings, including the Suleymaniye in Istanbul and the Selimiye Mosque in Edirne.

name: Ibn Zuhr
title: Physician of Seville
bio: A physician of Al-Andalus (d. 1162 CE) who wrote on diseases and treatment and stressed careful observation and experiment in medicine.

name: Ibn Tufayl
title: Author of Hayy ibn Yaqzan
bio: A physician and philosopher of Al-Andalus (d. 1185 CE) who wrote Hayy ibn Yaqzan, a story about a man raised alone on an island who finds truth through reason.

name: Jabir ibn Hayyan
title: Pioneer of Chemistry
bio: An early scholar, linked to the 8th century CE, to whom many works on chemistry are attributed. They describe distillation and other laboratory methods.

name: Abu al-Wafa al-Buzjani
title: Mathematician of Baghdad
bio: A mathematician and astronomer (d. 998 CE) who developed trigonometry further and wrote a book on the arithmetic and geometry useful to craftsmen.

name: Hunayn ibn Ishaq
title: Translator of the House of Wisdom
bio: A Christian physician from Hira (d. 873 CE) who led the translation of Greek medical and scientific works into Arabic in Abbasid Baghdad.

name: Az-Zarqali
title: Astronomer of Toledo
bio: An astronomer of Al-Andalus (d. 1100 CE) who improved the astrolabe and compiled the Toledan Tables used by astronomers across Europe.

name: Al-Jahiz
title: Master of Arabic Prose
bio: A writer of Basra (d. 868 CE) who wrote on animals, society and language. His Kitab al-Hayawan is a large book on the animal kingdom.

name: Ibn al-Baytar
title: Botanist of Malaga
bio: A botanist and pharmacist from Malaga (d. 1248 CE) who gathered knowledge about thousands of plants in his large book on simple drugs.

name: The Kaaba
title: The House of Allah
bio: The cube-shaped sanctuary at the center of the Sacred Mosque in Mecca, built by Ibrahim and Ismail. Muslims all over the world face it in prayer.

name: Al-Masjid al-Haram
title: The Sacred Mosque of Mecca
bio: The largest mosque in the world, surrounding the Kaaba. Pilgrims perform the tawaf here during Hajj and Umrah.

name: Al-Masjid an-Nabawi
title: The Prophet's Mosque
bio: The mosque built by the Prophet ﷺ in Medina after the Hijrah. It holds his resting place and is the second holiest mosque in Islam.

name: Al-Masjid al-Aqsa
title: The Farthest Mosque
bio: The mosque in Jerusalem that was the first qibla of the Muslims and the destination of the Prophet's Night Journey. It is the third holiest site in Islam.

name: The Well of Zamzam
title: The Blessed Spring
bio: The spring beside the Kaaba that gushed out for Hajar and her son Ismail. Pilgrims drink from it to this day.

name: The Black Stone
title: Start of the Tawaf
bio: The stone set in the eastern corner of the Kaaba. Pilgrims begin and end each circuit of the tawaf at its corner, and the Prophet ﷺ kissed it.

name: Maqam Ibrahim
title: The Station of Ibrahim
bio: The stone that Ibrahim stood on while building the Kaaba. The Quran tells the believers to take it as a place of prayer.

name: Safa and Marwa
title: The Running of Hajar
bio: Two hills near the Kaaba between which Hajar ran searching for water for Ismail. Pilgrims walk between them in the rite called sa'i.

name: The Plain of Arafat
title: The Day of Arafah
bio: The plain near Mecca where pilgrims gather on the ninth of Dhul-Hijjah. Standing at Arafat is the essence of the Hajj, and the Prophet ﷺ gave his farewell sermon here.

name: Mina
title: The Valley of the Pilgrims
bio: A valley near Mecca where the pilgrims stay during the days of Hajj and where they throw pebbles at the three pillars in memory of Ibrahim.

name: The Cave of Hira
title: Where the Quran Began
bio: A small cave on Jabal an-Nur above Mecca where the Prophet ﷺ used to retreat and where the first verses of the Quran were revealed to him.

name: The Cave of Thawr
title: Shelter of the Hijrah
bio: A cave on a mountain south of Mecca where the Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr hid for three days on the way to Medina while the Quraysh searched for them.

name: Ar-Rawda ash-Sharifa
title: The Garden of Paradise
bio: The area in the Prophet's Mosque between his house and his pulpit, which he described as a garden from the gardens of Paradise.

name: Quba Mosque
title: The First Mosque
bio: The mosque on the edge of Medina that the Prophet ﷺ founded on arriving there in 622 CE. A visit and prayer there are highly rewarded.

name: Masjid al-Qiblatayn
title: The Mosque of Two Qiblas
bio: The mosque in Medina where, according to tradition, the Muslims turned in the middle of their prayer from facing Jerusalem to facing the Kaaba.

name: The Valley of Badr
title: Site of the First Great Battle
bio: A place with wells on the road between Mecca and Medina where the Muslims won the Battle of Badr in 2 AH.

name: Mount Uhud
title: The Mountain That Loves Us
bio: The mountain north of Medina where the battle of Uhud took place. The Prophet ﷺ said that it is a mountain that loves us and that we love.

name: Al-Baqi Cemetery
title: Cemetery of the Companions
bio: The cemetery of Medina where many of the Prophet's family and companions are buried, including Uthman and many other early Muslims.

name: The Dome of the Rock
title: The Golden Dome
bio: The shrine built in Jerusalem in 691-692 CE under Abd al-Malik. It is one of the oldest surviving works of Islamic architecture.

name: The Umayyad Mosque
title: Pride of Damascus
bio: The Great Mosque of Damascus, built in the early 8th century CE on the site of an older church. It is among the oldest large stone mosques in the world.

name: The Great Mosque of Cordoba
title: The Forest of Columns
bio: The mosque begun by Abd ar-Rahman I in 785 CE and enlarged by his successors. Its hall of double arches in red and white is a landmark of Islamic Spain.

name: The Alhambra
title: The Red Fortress
bio: The palace and fortress of the Nasrid rulers of Granada, built mostly in the 13th and 14th centuries CE and famous for its courtyards, tilework and carved stucco.

name: Hagia Sophia
title: The Great Dome
bio: Built as a cathedral in 537 CE, it became a mosque after the Ottoman conquest of Constantinople in 1453. It later served as a museum and has been a mosque again since 2020.

name: The Suleymaniye Mosque
title: Masterpiece of Sinan
bio: The mosque in Istanbul built by Sinan for Suleiman the Magnificent and completed in 1557 CE. It dominates the skyline of the city.

name: The Selimiye Mosque
title: Sinan's Greatest Work
bio: The mosque in Edirne completed in 1575 CE, which Sinan called his masterpiece. Its great dome rises over a single large prayer hall.

name: Al-Azhar
title: The Radiant Mosque
bio: The mosque founded in Cairo in 970-972 CE that grew into one of the world's most important centers of Islamic learning.

name: Al-Qarawiyyin
title: Oldest Place of Learning
bio: The mosque and school founded in Fez in 859 CE by Fatima al-Fihri. It is considered one of the oldest continuously operating educational institutions in the world.

name: The Great Mosque of Kairouan
title: The Mosque of Uqba
bio: Founded by Uqba ibn Nafi around 670 CE in Kairouan, it took its present shape in the 9th century CE and became a model for the mosques of North Africa.

name: The Zaytuna Mosque
title: Mosque of the Olive
bio: The great mosque of Tunis, founded in the early 8th century CE. Its school trained generations of scholars of the Maghreb.

name: The Great Mosque of Tlemcen
title: Almoravid Mosque of Algeria
bio: Founded in 1082 CE by the Almoravid ruler Yusuf ibn Tashfin and completed in the following decades, it is one of the oldest mosques in Algeria.

name: The Qal'a of Beni Hammad
title: The Hammadid Capital
bio: The ruins of the capital founded in 1007 CE by the Hammadid ruler in the mountains of M'Sila in Algeria, a site that UNESCO has listed as a World Heritage Site.

name: Mecca
title: Birthplace of the Prophet
bio: The holiest city of Islam, where the Prophet ﷺ was born, where the Kaaba stands, and where the Quran began to be revealed.

name: Medina
title: The Radiant City
bio: The city formerly called Yathrib, which received the Prophet ﷺ after the Hijrah and became the first capital of the Muslim state.

name: Jerusalem
title: Al-Quds
bio: A holy city for the three Abrahamic faiths. For Muslims it is the site of al-Aqsa, the first qibla and the destination of the Night Journey.

name: Baghdad
title: City of Peace
bio: The capital of the Abbasid caliphate, founded in 762 CE, where the House of Wisdom stood and where many of the great scholars of Islam lived and taught.

name: Cordoba
title: Jewel of Al-Andalus
bio: The capital of Muslim Spain, with libraries, schools and a great mosque, which became one of the largest and most learned cities of medieval Europe.
