name: Timbuktu
title: City of Manuscripts
bio: A city on the edge of the Sahara that became a center of Islamic learning in the 14th to 16th centuries CE, with thousands of manuscripts and the scholars of Sankore.

name: Samarkand
title: Jewel of the Silk Road
bio: A great city of Central Asia that was a center of trade and science, where Ulugh Beg built his observatory and where Timur made his capital.

name: Bukhara
title: City of the Imams
bio: A city in Central Asia that was a major center of Islamic learning and the birthplace of Imam al-Bukhari in 810 CE.

name: Khubayb ibn Adi
title: Steadfast at Ar-Raji'
bio: A companion captured at Ar-Raji' and sold to the Quraysh in Mecca. Before his execution he asked to pray two rak'ahs, which became the practice of those facing death for their faith.

name: Abu Dujana al-Ansari
title: Bearer of the Prophet's Sword
bio: A brave fighter of the Ansar who was given the Prophet's sword at Uhud and protected him with his own body. He was martyred at the Battle of Yamama.

name: Hanzala ibn Abi Amir
title: Washed by the Angels
bio: A young companion who left his bride on his wedding night to join the Muslim army at Uhud. He was martyred there and is known as Ghasil al-Mala'ika.

name: Anas ibn an-Nadr
title: Uncle of Anas ibn Malik
bio: A companion who missed Badr and vowed to show what he could do in the next battle. He fought bravely at Uhud and was found with dozens of wounds.

name: Khuzayma ibn Thabit
title: The Man of Two Testimonies
bio: A companion of the Ansar whose single testimony the Prophet ﷺ declared equal to the testimony of two men. He later helped to confirm the verses of the Quran.

name: Al-Bara ibn Malik
title: Fearless Brother of Anas
bio: A brave fighter of the Ansar and brother of Anas ibn Malik. His courage in the garden of death at Yamama helped to turn the battle.

name: Thumama ibn Uthal
title: Chief of Yamama
bio: A chief of the Banu Hanifa who was captured, treated kindly by the Prophet ﷺ and accepted Islam. He stayed loyal and urged his people not to follow Musaylima.

name: Abu Basir
title: Free Man After Hudaybiyyah
bio: A Muslim of Mecca who escaped to Medina after the treaty of Hudaybiyyah and was sent back, then gathered a group on the coast who threatened Qurayshi caravans.

name: Abdullah ibn Hudhafa as-Sahmi
title: Envoy to Khosrow
bio: A companion who carried the letter of the Prophet ﷺ to Khosrow, ruler of Persia. He later fought in the Muslim armies and was held prisoner by the Byzantines.

name: Dihya al-Kalbi
title: Envoy to Heraclius
bio: A companion known for his beauty who carried the Prophet's letter to Heraclius. It is reported that the angel Jibril sometimes came to the Prophet ﷺ in his appearance.

name: Hatib ibn Abi Balta'a
title: Envoy to Egypt
bio: A companion who fought at Badr and carried the Prophet's letter to the ruler of Egypt, who sent back gifts and replied politely.

name: Salama ibn al-Akwa'
title: The Swift Archer
bio: A companion known for his speed on foot and skill with the bow. He was a hero of the expedition of Dhu Qarad and pledged under the tree at Hudaybiyyah.

name: Zayd ibn Arqam
title: Young Narrator of Medina
bio: A young companion from the Khazraj who joined many expeditions and narrated hadiths. He settled in Kufa and was among the well-known narrators there.

name: Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum
title: The Blind Muadhdhin
bio: A blind early convert who served as a muadhdhin alongside Bilal. The Prophet ﷺ left him in charge of Medina several times when he went out on expeditions.

name: Abu Bakra
title: Lowered From the Wall of Ta'if
bio: A servant who left the besieged town of Ta'if by lowering himself in a basket, and joined the Prophet ﷺ. He later settled in Basra and narrated hadiths.

name: Umm Atiyya al-Ansariyya
title: Nurse of the Army
bio: A woman of the Ansar who went out with the Muslim army on seven expeditions, cooking, caring for the wounded and treating the sick.

name: Asma bint Umays
title: Emigrant to Abyssinia
bio: A woman who migrated to Abyssinia with her husband Ja'far, and later married Abu Bakr and then Ali. She was known for her knowledge and patience.

name: Umm Hani bint Abi Talib
title: Cousin of the Prophet
bio: A cousin of the Prophet ﷺ who gave protection to two men at the conquest of Mecca, and whose protection he honored.

name: Abu Ubayd ath-Thaqafi
title: Commander of the Bridge
bio: A companion sent by Umar to lead the army in Iraq, who was martyred in 634 CE in the Battle of the Bridge against the Persians.

name: Dirar ibn al-Azwar
title: Horseman of Khalid
bio: A brave horseman and poet who fought under Khalid ibn al-Walid in the conquest of Syria and was known for charging the enemy ranks.

name: Amr ibn Ma'dikarib
title: Warrior-Poet of Yemen
bio: A famous warrior and poet of the tribe of Zubayd who accepted Islam and fought bravely at al-Qadisiyyah.

name: Sa'id ibn Amir al-Jumahi
title: Governor of Homs
bio: A companion appointed by Umar as governor of Homs, who was known for his simple life and for giving away his salary to the poor.

name: Ibn Ishaq
title: First Biographer of the Prophet
bio: A scholar of Medina (d. around 151 AH) who wrote the earliest major biography of the Prophet ﷺ, which later survived through the edition of Ibn Hisham.

name: Ibn Hisham
title: Editor of the Sira
bio: A scholar of Basra and Egypt (d. 218 AH) who edited and preserved the biography of the Prophet ﷺ by Ibn Ishaq. It is known as Sirat Ibn Hisham.

name: Ibn Sa'd
title: Author of at-Tabaqat
bio: A scholar of Baghdad (d. 230 AH) who wrote at-Tabaqat al-Kubra, a large biographical collection about the companions, Tabi'un and the Prophet's life.

name: Al-Baladhuri
title: Historian of the Conquests
bio: A historian of Baghdad (d. around 892 CE) who wrote Futuh al-Buldan, an early account of the Muslim conquests.

name: Ibn al-Athir
title: Author of al-Kamil
bio: A historian from Jazira who lived in Mosul (d. 630 AH). His al-Kamil fi at-Tarikh is a leading source for the history of Islam up to his time.

name: Ibn Khallikan
title: Author of Wafayat al-A'yan
bio: A scholar and judge (d. 681 AH) who compiled the Wafayat al-A'yan, a large dictionary of famous people in the history of Islam.

name: Al-Maqrizi
title: Historian of Egypt
bio: A historian of Cairo (d. 845 AH) who wrote about the topography and history of Egypt and the Mamluk state.

name: Ibn Manzur
title: Author of Lisan al-Arab
bio: A scholar (d. 711 AH) who compiled Lisan al-Arab, one of the largest dictionaries of the Arabic language.

name: Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad
title: Founder of Arabic Lexicography
bio: A scholar of Basra (d. around 170 AH) who wrote the first Arabic dictionary, Kitab al-Ayn, and created the science of Arabic prosody.

name: Sibawayh
title: Master of Arabic Grammar
bio: A scholar of Basra (d. around 180 AH) whose book on Arabic grammar, known simply as al-Kitab, became the foundation of the field.

name: Abu Ubayd al-Qasim ibn Sallam
title: Scholar of Language and Law
bio: A scholar (d. 224 AH) who wrote on the Quran, hadith, language and fiqh, including the Kitab al-Amwal on the finances of the early Muslim state.

name: Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad
title: Grandson of Abu Bakr
bio: One of the seven jurists of Medina, a grandson of Abu Bakr who was raised by his aunt Aisha and became a leading Tabi'i of the city.

name: Sulayman ibn Yasar
title: Jurist of Medina
bio: A freed servant of Maymuna and one of the seven jurists of Medina, respected for his knowledge and his piety.

name: Rabi'a ar-Ra'y
title: Teacher of Imam Malik
bio: A jurist of Medina (d. 136 AH) known for his sound reasoning and a teacher of Malik ibn Anas.

name: Hafsa bint Sirin
title: Female Scholar of Basra
bio: A Tabi'iyya of Basra, sister of Muhammad ibn Sirin, who was admired for her worship and memory of the Quran. Early scholars studied with her.

name: Umm ad-Darda as-Sughra
title: Jurist of Damascus
bio: A woman scholar of the Tabi'un who taught in Damascus and Jerusalem. The caliph Abd al-Malik sat among her students.

name: Karima al-Marwaziyya
title: Narrator of Sahih al-Bukhari
bio: A woman hadith scholar who lived in Mecca (d. 463 AH) and whose narration of Sahih al-Bukhari was highly valued by later scholars.

name: Abu Ya'la al-Farra'
title: Hanbali Jurist of Baghdad
bio: A leading Hanbali scholar of Baghdad (d. 458 AH) who wrote on fiqh and creed and trained many of the scholars who carried the school forward.

name: Abd al-Qadir al-Jilani
title: Preacher of Baghdad
bio: A Hanbali scholar and preacher of Baghdad (d. 561 AH) who attracted many followers by his sermons on sincerity and repentance.

name: Safi ar-Rahman al-Mubarakpuri
title: Author of ar-Raheeq al-Makhtum
bio: An Indian scholar (d. 1427 AH) whose Arabic biography of the Prophet ﷺ, ar-Raheeq al-Makhtum, won a prize and became widely read.

name: The Year of the Elephant
title: The Army That Came for the Kaaba
bio: Around 570 CE Abraha, the ruler of Yemen, marched on Mecca with an army and elephants to destroy the Kaaba. The Quran tells that Allah destroyed his army. The Prophet ﷺ was born in this year.

name: The Pact of the Virtuous
title: Justice Before Islam
bio: A pact made in Mecca before the revelation by several clans to defend the wronged and protect strangers. The young Muhammad ﷺ took part, and he later said he would answer such a call even in Islam.

name: The Rebuilding of the Kaaba
title: Placing the Black Stone
bio: Around 605 CE the Quraysh rebuilt the Kaaba. When they disputed who should lift the Black Stone into place, Muhammad ﷺ settled it by placing it on a cloth carried by the leaders of all the clans.

name: The Boycott of Banu Hashim
title: Three Years in the Valley
bio: For about three years the Quraysh boycotted the clans of Banu Hashim and Banu al-Muttalib, who supported the Prophet ﷺ, cutting off trade and marriage and forcing them to live in a valley outside Mecca.

name: The Year of Sorrow
title: Loss of Khadija and Abu Talib
bio: In the tenth year of the revelation the Prophet ﷺ lost his wife Khadija and his uncle Abu Talib, his two main sources of support in Mecca. It became known as the Year of Sorrow.

name: The Journey to Ta'if
title: A Prayer in the Midst of Hardship
bio: After the Year of Sorrow the Prophet ﷺ went to Ta'if hoping for support. The leaders rejected him and drove him out. He answered with patience and a famous prayer.

name: The First Pledge of al-Aqaba
title: Twelve Men of Medina
bio: In 621 CE a group of twelve men from Medina met the Prophet ﷺ at al-Aqaba and pledged to worship Allah alone. Mus'ab ibn Umayr was sent with them to teach Islam in Medina.

name: Battle of Jalula
title: Victory in Iraq
bio: Around 637 CE a Muslim army led by Hashim ibn Utba defeated the Persians at Jalula in Iraq, after the victory of al-Qadisiyyah, opening the way into the Persian highlands.

name: The Battle of Tours
title: The Pavement of the Martyrs
bio: In 732 CE the army of Abd ar-Rahman al-Ghafiqi met the Frankish forces of Charles Martel between Tours and Poitiers. Abd ar-Rahman was killed and the Muslim army withdrew.

name: The Second Siege of Constantinople
title: The Siege of Maslama
bio: In 717-718 CE an Umayyad army and fleet under Maslama besieged Constantinople for a year. A hard winter, hunger and Byzantine fire forced the Muslims to withdraw.

name: The Conquest of Sindh
title: The Young General in India
bio: Around 711-712 CE Muhammad ibn al-Qasim defeated Raja Dahir and took Sindh. It was the first lasting Muslim rule in the Indian subcontinent.

name: The Battle of Nicopolis
title: Bayezid Against the Crusaders
bio: In 1396 CE the Ottoman army of Bayezid I defeated a large European crusading army on the Danube, which strengthened Ottoman rule in the Balkans.

name: The Conquest of Cyprus
title: The First Muslim Naval Expedition
bio: Around 649 CE, in the time of Uthman, Mu'awiya led the first Muslim naval expedition to Cyprus. Umm Haram bint Milhan took part and died on the island.

name: The Founding of Kairouan
title: The First City of the Maghreb
bio: Around 670 CE Uqba ibn Nafi founded Kairouan in what is now Tunisia as a base for the conquest of North Africa. It became a center of Islamic learning.

name: The Founding of Marrakesh
title: The Almoravid Capital
bio: Around 1070 CE the Almoravids founded Marrakesh as their new capital in Morocco, from where Yusuf ibn Tashfin ruled a state reaching into Al-Andalus.

name: The Battle of the Three Kings
title: Victory in Morocco
bio: In 1578 CE the Saadian army defeated the Portuguese invasion at Wadi al-Makhazin in Morocco. King Sebastian of Portugal and two Moroccan rulers died in the battle.

name: The Battle of Annual
title: Victory of the Rif
bio: In 1921 CE the fighters of Abd el-Krim al-Khattabi defeated a Spanish army at Annual in the Rif mountains of Morocco, a major blow to colonial rule.

name: The Battle of Sidi Brahim
title: A Victory of Emir Abdelkader
bio: In September 1845 CE the forces of Emir Abdelkader destroyed a French column near Ghazaouet in western Algeria, one of the most famous victories of his resistance.

name: Abdul-Muttalib
title: Grandfather of the Prophet
bio: The chief of Quraysh and grandfather of the Prophet ﷺ. He rediscovered the well of Zamzam and cared for his orphaned grandson until his own death.

name: Halima as-Sa'diyya
title: Nurse of the Prophet
bio: A woman of the tribe of Banu Sa'd who nursed and raised the infant Muhammad ﷺ in the desert during his early years, a custom of the Arabs of Mecca.

name: Abu Quhafa
title: Father of Abu Bakr
bio: The father of Abu Bakr, who accepted Islam at the conquest of Mecca. He lived to see his son become the first caliph.

name: Umm Ruman
title: Mother of Aisha
bio: The wife of Abu Bakr and mother of Aisha and Abd ar-Rahman. She accepted Islam early, migrated to Medina and passed away during the lifetime of the Prophet ﷺ.

name: Yasir ibn Amir
title: Tortured for His Faith
bio: The father of Ammar and husband of Sumayyah. The family was tortured by the Quraysh for their faith, and Yasir died from the ill-treatment in Mecca.

name: Larbi Tebessi
title: Scholar of the Revolution
bio: An Algerian scholar (d. 1957) and secretary of the Association of Algerian Muslim Scholars, who supported the independence struggle and was abducted by French forces in 1957.

name: Tayeb el-Okbi
title: Reformer and Journalist
bio: An Algerian scholar (d. 1960) who worked with Ben Badis to renew religious education, and edited reformist newspapers in Algiers.

name: Mubarak al-Mili
title: Historian of Algeria
bio: An Algerian scholar (d. 1945) and member of the reform movement who wrote a history of Algeria from earliest times and a treatise on polytheism and its forms.

name: Cheikh Bouamama
title: Leader of the South
bio: A religious and military leader who led the resistance against French rule in southwestern Algeria from 1881 and continued the struggle until his death in 1908.

name: Cheikh Aheddad
title: Leader of the 1871 Revolt
bio: A leader of the Rahmaniyya order in Kabylia (d. 1873) who called for jihad in 1871 and supported Mokrani's revolt against French rule.

name: Mohamed El Mokrani
title: Leader of the 1871 Revolt
bio: A Kabyle chief who led the great uprising against French rule in 1871. He was killed in May of that year at Oued Soufflat.

name: Abdulhamid II
title: Sultan of the Hejaz Railway
bio: The Ottoman sultan from 1876 to 1909 who supported projects such as the Hejaz Railway, which linked Damascus to Medina and made the pilgrimage easier.

name: Murad II
title: Victor of Varna
bio: The Ottoman sultan (d. 1451 CE) who defeated a crusading army at Varna in 1444 CE and was the father of Muhammad al-Fatih.

name: Abd al-Ghani al-Maqdisi
title: Author of Umdat al-Ahkam
bio: A Hanbali hadith scholar (d. 600 AH) born in Palestine and a cousin of Ibn Qudama. His Umdat al-Ahkam, a short collection of hadith, is memorized by students.

name: Ibn Abi Hatim ar-Razi
title: Critic of Narrators
bio: A hadith scholar of Rayy (d. 327 AH) who wrote a commentary on the Quran based on narrations and al-Jarh wa't-Ta'dil, on the reliability of narrators.

name: Abu Zur'a ar-Razi
title: Master of Hadith Criticism
bio: A hadith critic of Rayy (d. 264 AH) known for his memory and his strict standards in judging narrators. He is often named together with Abu Hatim.

name: Muhammad ibn Isma'il as-San'ani
title: Author of Subul as-Salam
bio: A Yemeni scholar (d. 1182 AH) who wrote Subul as-Salam, a commentary on a collection of hadiths about legal rulings, and called for following the proofs.

name: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim Al ash-Shaykh
title: First Grand Mufti
bio: A scholar of Riyadh (d. 1389 AH) who served as the first Grand Mufti of Saudi Arabia and supervised the growth of religious education in the country.

name: Abu Bakr al-Jaza'iri
title: Teacher of the Prophet's Mosque
bio: An Algerian scholar (d. 2018) who taught for decades in the Prophet's Mosque in Medina and wrote Aysar at-Tafasir and Minhaj al-Muslim.

name: Al-Mawardi
title: Author of al-Ahkam as-Sultaniyya
bio: A Shafi'i jurist and judge of Baghdad (d. 450 AH) who wrote al-Ahkam as-Sultaniyya, a classic work on the principles of government and public law.

name: Al-Muqaddasi
title: Geographer of Jerusalem
bio: A geographer born in Jerusalem (d. around 990 CE) who traveled through Muslim lands and wrote Ahsan at-Taqasim, a detailed description of their regions and peoples.

name: Ibn Hawqal
title: Traveler and Geographer
bio: A traveler from Nisibis who journeyed for decades across Africa and Asia in the 10th century CE and wrote Surat al-Ard, a geographical work with maps.

name: Ibn Yunus
title: Astronomer of Cairo
bio: An Egyptian astronomer (d. 1009 CE) who compiled the Hakimi Zij, a table of astronomical observations of great accuracy, using his own measurements.

name: Thabit ibn Qurra
title: Mathematician of Harran
bio: A scholar of Baghdad (d. 901 CE) who translated and improved works of Greek mathematics, and wrote on geometry, astronomy and mechanics.

name: Ibn ash-Shatir
title: Timekeeper of the Umayyad Mosque
bio: An astronomer of Damascus (d. around 1375 CE) who worked as timekeeper of the Umayyad Mosque and developed models of planetary motion that later astronomers studied.

name: Taqi ad-Din
title: Astronomer of Istanbul
bio: A scholar born in Damascus (d. 1585 CE) who built an observatory in Istanbul in 1577 CE and built mechanical clocks and instruments.

name: Evliya Celebi
title: The Great Ottoman Traveler
bio: An Ottoman traveler (d. after 1682 CE) who spent about forty years journeying through the empire and beyond and wrote the ten-volume Seyahatname.

name: Ibn Bajja
title: Philosopher of Saragossa
bio: A philosopher, physician and musician of Al-Andalus (d. 1138 CE), known in Europe as Avempace, who wrote on logic, astronomy and the soul.

name: The Ibrahimi Mosque
title: The Sanctuary of Ibrahim
bio: The mosque in Hebron built over the cave traditionally believed to be the burial place of Ibrahim and several other prophets and their families.

name: The Great Mosque of Samarra
title: The Spiral Minaret
bio: The mosque built in Samarra in the 9th century CE by the Abbasid caliph al-Mutawakkil. Its famous spiral minaret, the Malwiya, still stands.

name: The Mosque of Ibn Tulun
title: The Oldest Mosque of Cairo
bio: The mosque built in Cairo between 876 and 879 CE by Ahmad ibn Tulun. It is one of the largest and oldest mosques in Egypt that survives in its original form.

name: The Mosque of Sidi Okba
title: Tomb of Uqba ibn Nafi
bio: A mosque near Biskra in Algeria, built around the grave traditionally believed to be that of Uqba ibn Nafi, the commander who died in the region in 683 CE.

name: The Great Mosque of Djenne
title: The Mud Mosque of Mali
bio: A mosque in Mali built of mud brick, said to be the largest building of this type in the world. The present building dates from 1907 and is rebuilt with mud every year.

name: The Taj Mahal
title: Marble Monument of Love
bio: The mausoleum built in Agra by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan between 1632 and 1653 CE for his wife Mumtaz Mahal, a masterpiece of Islamic architecture in India.
